title: Associate Director, Clinical Sciences
description:
About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Associate Director, Clinical Sciences, you'll help translate Hemab's science into well-designed clinical studies and reliable evidence about how our treatments perform in patients. You'll have hands-on scientific ownership across protocol development, study execution and data review, working closely with Medical Directors and colleagues across clinical development.

What you'll do

  • Drive the clinical science contribution to study design and execution, bringing clinical data and scientific thinking into development decisions.
  • Lead protocol development with the Medical Director, including amendments as study needs and emerging data change.
  • Review clinical study data, resolve discrepancies and identify safety or efficacy trends that need investigation or action.
  • Develop study documents and plans, including informed consent forms, eCRFs, medical monitoring plans and data review plans.
  • Guide sites and vendors on protocol requirements, eligibility criteria and participant management so the study is executed as intended.
  • Work with clinical development colleagues to analyse and interpret study results and build a clear picture of what the data are telling us.
  • Help communicate study findings clearly to internal and external stakeholders alongside the Medical Director.
  • Contribute clinical content to regulatory documents, including investigator brochures, annual safety reports, clinical study reports and registration submissions.

What you'll bring to Hemab

  • Significant experience in clinical science or clinical research within drug development, including direct involvement in interventional clinical studies.
  • Experience developing clinical protocols and reviewing and interpreting clinical study data.
  • A strong working understanding of ICH-GCP, clinical study design and drug development in a regulated environment.
  • The ability to interpret clinical information, scientific literature and changing treatment approaches and apply it to clinical development decisions.
  • Experience working closely with cross-functional colleagues and external partners, including investigators, consultants or vendors.

Nice to have

  • Experience in haematology, rare disease or bleeding disorders.
  • Experience working across different stages of drug development, from early development towards registration.
  • An advanced scientific or clinical degree.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

This is the actual shape of working somewhere at this stage: It's genuinely energising for the right person and genuinely frustrating for the wrong one. If you want a place where the operating manual is already written, this might not be it – but if you want to help write it, this might be exactly it.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Hemab Therapeutics is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

title: Wave Planner
description:
The Wave Planner decides what work hits the distribution center floor and when. You release orders for the entire Jay Group network, build and run waves in our Manhattan warehouse management system (WMS), and make sure every package leaving the LCO facility is labeled correctly and out the door before the carrier cutoff. You are also the person who takes on order research when something does not look right, and gets it resolved.

This is a high-visibility role for someone who is organized, precise, and genuinely enjoys solving problems. You will work side by side with Client Services, Shipping, and Operations, and you will become one of the most capable WMS users in the building. Prior wave planning experience is a plus, but attention to detail, comfort with systems, and the drive to learn matter most.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities (other duties may be assigned as business needs change)

Wave Planning and Order Release:

  • Build, run, and release waves daily in the WMS so work reaches the DC floor on time and in the right sequence.

  • Perform order research: investigate orders that need attention, determine the root cause, and get them moving.

  • Reconcile every wave for the ship day to confirm all waves are manifested and invoiced.

  • Escalate any manifest that cannot be closed to the Team Lead and Shipping Supervisor, with the detail needed to resolve it.

  • Assist with general inventory and order reconciliation efforts.

Shipping, Manifesting, and Carrier Compliance

  • Process outgoing small parcel shipments using the Manhattan WMS, FedEx Ship Manager, UPS WorldShip, and other carrier systems.

  • Ensure the LCO operation meets every daily carrier cutoff.

  • Prepare bills of lading and other documentation required for LTL shipments, following established carrier relationships and client specifications.

  • Examine outgoing shipments to confirm they meet client and carrier specifications.

  • Identify and sort small parcel shipping labels by carrier, and attach packing lists to carton picks staged at shipping.

  • Read collates to determine the quantity and type of transportation required, and load trucks as needed.

  • Troubleshoot and maintain the printers used in the waving and labeling process.

Communication and Problem Solving

  • Communicate daily with the Client Services team on issues and risks so customer service levels stay high.

  • Partner with other departments to ensure client requirements and expectations are met.

  • Identify problems, determine root cause, and drive them to resolution rather than passing them along.

  • Provide an end-of-day summary of shipments and open issues that will carry over to the oncoming shift.

Safety and Work Area

  • Operate material handling equipment safely: complete required training, follow prescribed safety regulations, and maintain safety inspection logs.

  • Maintain 5S standards in the shipping department.

What Success Looks Like:

  • First 30 days: running standard daily waves independently and consistently meeting carrier cutoffs.

  • First 60 days: handling order research, label problems, and printer issues without escalation.

  • First 90 days: recognized as a WMS power user — the person the floor comes to when something does not look right.

description:

Human Capital — HC Forward
The Human Capital Offering Portfolio helps organizations manage and sustain their performance through their most important asset: their people. We see Human Capital as a topic critical to the C-Suite, and we bring together technology, insights, and services to help our clients innovate faster and proactively drive their business strategies.
HC Forward is Deloitte’s innovation engine for Human Capital — integrating technology, data, and industry expertise to create scalable solutions and assets that extend client capabilities and drive ongoing value across all Human Capital offerings.
About Intelligent Payroll
Intelligent Payroll is an HC Forward platform that uses machine learning to detect anomalies, forecast variances, and reduce manual intervention in enterprise payroll processing. It runs on Azure, ingests data from multiple HRIS sources (SAP, Oracle, ADP, Workday), normalises it into a common data model, and serves both batch ML pipelines and rule-based validation engines.
This is a builder role. You will spend your time writing production Python code, designing pipelines, and shipping features. You will not be in client workshops, executive presentations, or pre-sales.
Data Scientist, 5-8 years experience,


Work you’ll do
∙Design and ship distributed data processing pipelines in PySpark, moving raw payroll data through a medallion architecture (raw → standardised → aggregated → modelled)
∙Build ML pipelines for time-series forecasting and anomaly detection over payroll data
∙Write clean, class-based, testable Python — interfaces, factories, dependency injection, not 800-line procedural scripts
∙Submit and orchestrate Spark jobs programmatically on a managed cloud ML platform (we use Azure ML Studio, but the patterns generalise)












∙Own the contracts between subsystems: data pipelines, ML libraries, and orchestration layers are intentionally decoupled, and you will help keep them that way
∙Write tests, write docs, review PRs, and treat the pipeline as a product, not a notebook

These are non-negotiable. If you don’t have these, this isn’t the right role.
Production PySpark
∙You have shipped PySpark code that ran in production — not just one notebook, but a pipeline that processed real data on a recurring schedule.
∙You know the DataFrame API, schema validation, parquet I/O, partitioning, and how to debug a job that’s slow or wrong.
∙You can write a PySpark job that runs locally for development and at scale in the cloud, without changing the business logic.
Strong Python & OOP
∙You write production Python by default: classes, modules, type hints, tests.
∙You know when to reach for an abstract base class, a factory, or dependency injection — and when not to.
∙You can read someone else’s class-based codebase and explain what it does, end to end.
Engineering experience

∙You ask about data quality before you ask about model choice.
∙You can work from a config file, a CLI entry point, and a YAML pipeline definition — not just python script.py.
Cloud ML platforms
∙You have submitted Spark or ML jobs programmatically using a cloud ML SDK (Azure ML, AWS SageMaker / boto3, Vertex AI) and understand cloud environments.
Data science fundamentals
∙Hands-on with core ML algorithms, with a solid grounding in regression.

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join the Enterprise Logging team and lead development of a next-generation log processing pipeline. This role is responsible for designing, building, and operating a high-throughput Lambda-based consumer that transforms and delivers ~500 TB/day of cloud log data from AWS, GCP, and Azure into Splunk Cloud. The ideal candidate has deep experience with streaming data systems, multi-cloud environments, and building production-grade data pipelines on a scale.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Design and develop a serverless event processing pipeline (AWS Lambda) that reads from Kinesis Data Streams, transforms events, and delivers CIM-compliant payloads to Splunk Cloud via HTTP Event Collector (HEC)
  • Implement event parsing and transformation logic across multiple cloud log formats (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, GCP Audit Logs, Azure Activity Logs, and others)
  • Build and maintain source/source type mapping configurations supporting 59,000+ unique log type combinations
  • Develop tiered data routing logic (Keep / Reduce / Skip) to optimize Splunk licensing costs
  • Implement timestamp extraction and normalization across heterogeneous event formats
  • Operate and monitor the pipeline in production - build observability dashboards, alerting, and error handling (dead-letter queues, retry logic)
  • Collaborate with the Centralized Logging team on Kinesis stream integration and Enhanced Fan-Out configuration
  • Participate in architecture decisions, code reviews, and CI/CD pipeline development
  • Write infrastructure as code (Terraform or CloudFormation) for all deployed components
  • Contribute data standards and onboarding documentation for new log sources
  • Comply with all applicable Company policies, procedures, and business directives, changes including those relating to work location, team assignments, work schedules, and flexible work arrangements

Required Qualifications:

  • Cloud Platforms (Multi-Cloud)
    • AWS (primary): Solid hands-on experience with Lambda, Kinesis Data Streams, S3, IAM, CloudWatch, PrivateLink, DynamoDB, and SQS
    • GCP: Working knowledge of Cloud Logging, Pub/Sub, IAM, and GCP audit log formats
    • Azure: Working knowledge of Event Hubs, Activity Logs, Diagnostic Logs, Storage Accounts, and Azure Monitor
  • Streaming & Data Engineering
    • Experience building high-throughput streaming pipelines (Kinesis, Kafka, or equivalent)
    • Experience with data serialization formats (JSON, AVRO, Protobuf) and compression (gzip, base64 encoding)
    • Understanding of event-driven architecture and at-least-once delivery semantics
    • Familiarity with fan-out patterns, backpressure handling, and shard-level parallelism
  • Software Development
    • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience
    • Experience with CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or equivalent)
    • Experience writing and maintaining infrastructure as code (Terraform preferred; CloudFormation acceptable)
    • Proficiency in Go (primary) with experience writing and maintaining production Lambda functions; the existing consumer is implemented in Go
    • Solid understanding of error handling patterns: exponential backoff, dead-letter queues, circuit breakers
    • Proficiency in Python (secondary) for tooling, automation, and supporting services
    • Proficiency with Git-based workflows, code review practices, and trunk-based development
  • Observability & Operations
    • Experience building monitoring and alerting data pipelines for production
    • Understanding of distributed systems failure modes and operational runbook development
    • Familiarity with CloudWatch Metrics, Logs, and Alarms (or equivalent observability stack)

What You'll Be Building

This is not a maintenance role. You will be building a greenfield, high-scale data pipeline that:

  • Processes ~500 TB/day across three major cloud providers
  • Transforms events from a legacy AVRO-wrapped format into CIM-compliant native payloads
  • Directly enables Splunk Enterprise Security detection capabilities (correlation searches, data model acceleration)
  • Implements intelligent data tiering to reduce licensing costs by tens of terabytes per day

At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and make the health system work better for everyone. We believe everyone-of every race, gender, sexuality, age, location and income-deserves the opportunity to live their healthiest life. Today, however, there are still far too many barriers to good health which are disproportionately experienced by people of color, historically marginalized groups and those with lower incomes. We are committed to mitigating our impact on the environment and enabling and delivering equitable care that addresses health disparities and improves health outcomes - an enterprise priority reflected in our mission.

title: Senior Technical Product Developer
description:
About Ruggable:

Ruggable is a leading direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand based in Los Angeles, California with an extraordinary track record of high, profitable growth. We pride ourselves on having an extremely loyal customer base and a talented team made up of genuinely caring people who take action and deliver results. We are venture-backed and own a patented washable rug design that's disrupting the home décor industry. Our mission is to empower our customers to live vibrantly with beautiful products that don't compromise on function. If you're passionate about consumer products, e-commerce, and high-growth start-ups, keep reading!

Job Summary: The Senior Technical Product Developer is responsible for leading the development and commercialization of rugs and home textile products for core product optimization and in-line product expansion. This role requires deep expertise in textile materials, yarns, constructions, manufacturing processes, testing, and product performance, combined with extensive experience working directly with overseas factories and suppliers. The ideal candidate has 10+ years of hands-on product development experience and can translate creative and commercial product direction into technically sound, scalable, cost-effective products. This individual will serve as a key technical resource across, Design, Product Management, Sourcing, Quality, Compliance, and Operations, proactively identifying risks and resolving complex development and production challenges

What You’ll Do
• Lead the development and commercialization of rugs and home textile products from concept/R&D handover through production handover.
• Translate design concepts and product briefs into detailed technical specifications, constructions, materials, performance requirements, and manufacturing solutions.
• Partner directly with overseas factories and suppliers to develop yarns, fibers, fabrics, backing systems, finishes, trims, and constructions that achieve the intended aesthetic, performance, quality, and cost objectives.
• Provide technical expertise across manufacturing processes including weaving, tufting, knitting, extrusion, bonding, coating, washing, dyeing, printing, finishing, and other relevant textile processes.
• Evaluate product constructions and recommend materials, processes, or engineering solutions that improve quality, performance, manufacturability, consistency, and cost.
• Own technical documentation throughout development, including product specifications, sample evaluations, construction details, testing requirements and results, pre-production trials, and final production standards.
• Review development samples and provide clear, technically actionable feedback to suppliers to drive efficient sample iterations and approvals.
• Proactively identify technical, quality, cost, and manufacturing risks and lead root-cause analysis and corrective actions when issues arise.
• Create detailed development timelines and critical-path milestones, partnering cross-functionally to ensure projects remain on schedule.
• Lead pre-production trials and commercialization activities to ensure approved products can be consistently replicated at production scale.
• Establish and maintain product quality and performance standards in partnership with Quality Assurance and Compliance teams.
• Build strong technical relationships with global suppliers and factories and challenge partners to continuously improve capabilities, quality, efficiency, innovation, and cost.
• Conduct factory visits, technical reviews, and development meetings with overseas suppliers as required.
• Partner with Sourcing on cost engineering and value-engineering initiatives while protecting product integrity, performance, and quality.
• Serve as a senior technical resource and mentor to Product team members, sharing expertise and helping strengthen technical capabilities across the organization.
• Drive continuous improvement in development processes, specifications, documentation, and supplier execution.

What You’ll Need to Have
Required
• Bachelor’s degree in Textiles, Textile Engineering, Industrial Design, Product Development, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent relevant industry experience may be considered.
• 10+ years of progressive technical product development experience, preferably within rugs, home textiles, floor coverings, or related textile categories.
• Extensive hands-on knowledge of textile materials, yarns, fibers, constructions, finishing techniques, and manufacturing processes.
• Demonstrated experience developing and commercializing products directly with overseas factories and suppliers.
• Strong understanding of manufacturing feasibility, cost engineering, product performance, quality, and production scalability.
• Proven ability to diagnose complex technical and manufacturing problems, identify root causes, and drive effective corrective solutions.
• Experience creating, reviewing, and maintaining detailed product specifications and technical documentation.
• Strong understanding of product testing, quality standards, and performance requirements.
• Excellent project-management skills with demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex development programs and critical timelines simultaneously.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical information effectively across creative, commercial, operational, and manufacturing teams.
• Ability to work independently, exercise sound technical judgment, and make decisions in a fast-paced development environment.
• Ability to collaborate effectively across Design, Product Management, Sourcing, Quality, Compliance, and Operations.
• Willingness to travel internationally to factories, suppliers, and trade shows.
• Ability to accommodate communication with global suppliers across multiple time zones.

Preferred
• Deep technical fabric expertise specifically within rug and floor-covering construction, including woven, tufted, machine-made, handwoven, printed, and other relevant constructions.
• Strong knowledge of yarn extrusion, spinning, dyeing, weaving, tufting, backing, bonding, coating, washing, finishing, and related processes.
• Experience working with natural and synthetic fibers and yarn systems.
• Working knowledge of ASTM, AATCC, ISO, and other relevant textile testing standards and protocols.
• Experience with PLM systems, technical specification systems, Airtable and project-management tools.
• Demonstrated experience in value engineering and product cost optimization.
• Experience evaluating and developing new factory capabilities, materials, technologies, and manufacturing processes

Compensation:
● $120,000-135,000 per year base salary based on experience
● An annual bonus percentage that varies based on level of role
● Employer matching (up to 3% of base salary) for company sponsored 401K plan

title: Senior Program Officer, Immediate Impact and Grantmaking
description:
About Us


The Cleveland Foundation, established in 1914 as the world’s first community foundation, continues to shape the future of place-based philanthropy more than a century later. With $4.2 billion in assets and a legacy of bold leadership, we are driven by a commitment to improve the lives of everyone who calls Greater Cleveland home, today and for generations to come.


Joining our team means becoming part of a culture that blends history-making impact with forward-looking innovation. Our vision is a vibrant Northeast Ohio where no Clevelander is left behind. Every team member plays a key role in advancing this vision by tackling Cleveland’s most critical issues, championing opportunities for all, and helping unlock the full potential of our region.


Our headquarters in the heart of MidTown places us at the center of a historic neighborhood and growing district, surrounded by partners, community leaders and residents who are reimagining what’s possible for our city. Here, you’ll work in a dynamic, collaborative environment designed to spark creativity, deepen relationships, and accelerate change.


At the Cleveland Foundation, you can be part of building a stronger future for every Clevelander.


About You


You are passionate about making a difference in your community and excited by the opportunity to contribute to meaningful change. You thrive when working collaboratively with diverse groups to solve complex challenges, and you have a proven ability to lead with integrity, foster inclusiveness, and innovate under pressure. You bring a forward-thinking mindset and a commitment to equity to everything you do, always ensuring your work drives social impact and results in tangible, positive outcomes.


Your best results come from thinking strategically while staying grounded in practical, results-oriented action. You analyze business trends and integrate insights to inform decision-making, identifying long-term opportunities and developing plans to seize them. As an excellent communicator and trusted partner, you can listen actively, seek to understand different perspectives, and apply innovative ideas to drive change. You possess a growth mindset, excel in team dynamics, and have a track record of applying entrepreneurial spirit to problem-solving, all while upholding the values of transparency, accountability, and collaboration.


Job Summary


The Senior Program Officer, Immediate Impact and Grantmaking plays a key role in strengthening the Foundation's grantmaking practice by bringing rigor, analysis, and clarity to grantmaking decisions. This role is responsible for managing a portfolio of grants, supporting day-to-day grantmaking processes, conducting due diligence, monitoring grant performance, and coordinating with colleagues across Grantmaking, Philanthropy, Finance, and other departments to advance effective grantmaking.


Reporting to the Vice President, Grantmaking, the Senior Program Officer serves as a trusted thought partner, helping translate strategy into grantmaking recommendations, navigate complex grant situations, identify emerging opportunities and challenges, and contribute to a culture of excellence, consistency, and learning across the Foundation's grantmaking work.


Key Responsibilities

  • Support the Foundation’s Immediate Impact grantmaking function, ensuring the investments are timely, rigorous, and aligned with the Impact Agenda and organizational priorities.
  • Acts as a responsive, strategic, well-respected and public-facing partner to non-profits who are seeking grants, exercising excellent communication skills and relationship building.
  • Delivers on key operational areas, including grant intake and portfolio assignments, reviewing grantmaking write-ups for rigor and clarity, ensures that grant reporting and metrics reporting is accurate and timely, and preparing board content in partnership with Grants Management.
  • Manages a portfolio of Immediate Impact grantees around a variety of issue areas and disciplines related to the Cleveland community’s wellbeing, critical needs and stabilization.
  • Acts as a senior problem-solver for complex or sensitive grant requests, bringing structure, judgment, and clear framing to ambiguous, high-risk, or high-stakes decisions.
  • Contributes to building a high-performing, disciplined, and learning-oriented grantmaking department by modeling strong judgment, thoughtful due diligence, resonant leadership, and respectful partner engagement.
  • Interprets and synthesizes grantmaking activity across immediate and long-term portfolios to identify patterns, themes, lessons, and tensions that inform leadership judgment and future decision making (sensemaking).
  • Partners with the Philanthropic Services team to introduce high-impact grantees to donors.
  • Helps refine, document, and socialize grantmaking guidelines, thresholds, and decision frameworks to improve transparency, consistency, and internal alignment across the department.
  • Prepare and present clear, compelling, and decision ready materials for foundation leadership, the Board and Board committees, including translating complex grantmaking information into concise narratives that support effective governance and strategic decision making.
  • Collaborate and coordinate across the impact team (including program and philanthropy), along with finance, communications, and operations to align immediate impact investments with available tools and resources.
  • Other duties as assigned by the Vice President, Grantmaking.

Competencies & Behavioral Expectations

  • Judgment
  • Communication
  • Commitment to Excellence
  • Teamwork & Collaboration
  • Adaptability
  • Problem-Solving
  • Strategy
  • Partnership

title: Spildevandsprøvetager – selvstændigt feltarbeje
description:
Eurofins Miljø A/S er et af Danmarks største miljølaboratorier. Vi arbejder med analyser af blandt andet vand, jord og luft og hjælper vores kunder med at passe på miljøet, fremme bæredygtighed og leve op til gældende krav. Hos os bliver du en del af en international virksomhed med en vigtig samfundsopgave – og et lokalt team i Vejen, hvor samarbejde, ansvar og god energi i hverdagen betyder meget.

Har du lyst til et selvstændigt job med frihed og ansvar?

Trives du bedst med at arbejde ude det meste af dagen, køre mellem forskellige lokationer og selv planlægge din dag?

Hos Eurofins søger vi en prøveudtager til spildevand, der kan arbejde selvstændigt i felten og trives med en varieret arbejdsdag, hvor ingen dage er ens.

Om jobbet

Som spildevandsprøvetager bliver du en del af vores team på Sjælland, men arbejder i høj grad selvstændigt i dagligdagen.

- Du kører alene fra site til site og udtager prøver
- Din arbejdsplads er bilen – som fungerer som dit mobile kontor
- Du arbejder udendørs og i forskellige miljøer
- Du har kontakt med kunder og repræsenterer Eurofins professionelt
- Du planlægger din egen arbejdsdag inden for de givne rammer

Du skal være indstillet på varierende arbejdsdage, udendørs arbejde året rundt samt mulighed for længere arbejdsdage og periodisk weekendarbejde.

Jobbet passer særligt godt til dig, der:

- Trives med at arbejde selvstændigt
- Er praktisk anlagt og komfortabel med fysisk arbejde
- Arbejder struktureret og kvalitetsbevidst
- Er fleksibel og kan bevare overblikket
- Har kørekort B

Din baggrund kan være teknisk, håndværksmæssig eller miljøfaglig – det vigtigste er din tilgang og motivation.

Hvad tilbyder vi?

- Et selvstændigt job med frihed under ansvar
- En varieret arbejdsdag i felten
- Grundig oplæring og mentorordning
- God sparring med planlægning og kollegaer
- En vigtig rolle i arbejdet med miljø og bæredygtighed

Arbejdstid
Dine 37 ugentlige arbejdstimer placeres normalt på hverdage. Der er mulighed for fleksible arbejdstider, dog skal det koordineres i samarbejde med planlægningsteamet. Der kan forekomme lange arbejdsdage, hvis der er hasteprøver. Der kan ligeledes forekomme arbejde i nogle weekender.

Arbejdssted
Du vil køre på Sjælland med udgangspunkt i Ringsted-området (primært Ringsted, Sorø og Slagelse).

Ansøgning
Hvis du synes det lyder interessant og som den rigtige mulighed for dig, så send dit CV og ansøgning ved at klikke på "Jeg er interesseret". Du skal søge online, det er eneste mulighed. Ansøgninger sendt på mail medtages ikke i puljen.

Udvælges du som en af de kandidater, vi ønsker at invitere med i rekrutteringsprocessen, vil du modtage et link til en kort videobesvarelse af nogle spørgsmål forud for en eventuel samtale.

Hvis du har spørgsmål til stillingen, kan du kontakte PBU Manager Per Andersen på mail: Per.Andersen@etn.eurofins.com

Du kan læse mere om Eurofins på

I forbindelse med rekrutteringen vil du blive bedt om at fremvise straffeattest og kørekort.

#TestingForLife

Eurofins Scientific er en international life science virksomhed, som tilbyder et unikt udvalg af analyser til kunder inden for mange forskellige industrier, med det formål at gøre livet og vores miljø mere sikkert, sundere og mere bæredygtigt. Fra den mad du spiser, til vandet du drikker, til medicinen du anvender, arbejder Eurofins sammen med de største virksomheder i verden, for at understøtte, at de produkter virksomhederne udbyder er sikre, deres ingredienser er autentiske og at mærkningen på produkterne er korrekte. Eurofins er verdensledende inden for test af fødevarer, miljø, farmaceutiske og kosmetiske produkter, samt agro-science CRO services. Eurofins er ydermere en af de globale markedsledere inden for specifikke test og laboratorieservices inden for genomics, farmakologi, retsmedicin, CDMO, avanceret materialevidenskab, samt support til kliniske studier.

På lidt mere end 30 år er Eurofins vokset fra at været et enkelt laboratorium i Nantes i Frankrig, til at bestå af 62.000 medarbejdere i et netværk af mere end 1000 selvstændige selskaber og 900 laboratorier i over 62 lande. Eurofins tilbyder en portefølje af mere end 200.000 analytiske metoder, til at evaluere sikkerhed, identitet, sammensætning, ægthed, oprindelse, sporbarhed og renhed af biologiske stoffer og produkter. Som en af de førende spillere inden for specialiseret klinisk diagnostisk test, tilbyder vi endvidere vi innovative klinisk diagnostiske testydelser.
I 2024 genererede Eurofins en samlet indtægt på 6,515 milliarder Euro og er i blandt de aktier, som har performet bedst i Europa over de sidste 20 år.

title: Admissions Coordinator
description:
The Admissions Coordinator supports the Administrator and the Admissions team with managing the administrative process for screening referrals, and residents entering our Behavioral Health Assisted Living community under the Specific Needs Contract. This role ensures that each admission meets Oregon Administrative Rule (OAR) requirements, Medicaid eligibility standards, and the behavioral and clinical criteria outlined by the State of Oregon.

The Admissions Coordinator acts as a liaison between hospitals, skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), Case Managers, behavioral health agencies, and the Oregon Department of Human Services (ODHS). This position also provides ongoing administrative and compliance support to the Administrator and Directors to support documentation, reporting, and regulatory requirements that are completed accurately and on time.

The Admissions Coordinator must also maintain strong communication, organization, and professional judgment in a fast-paced environment while demonstrating compassion, discretion, and respect for individuals with complex behavioral health needs.

Essential Job Functions

The information provided below encompasses the functions and capabilities linked with this position.

Duties and Responsibilities

The individual in this position is expected to engage in the following work-related activities.

  • Collaborate with Facility Manager, Maintenance, and housekeeping to ensure vacant rooms are move-in ready in an appropriate time frame.
  • Communicates bi-monthly with Case Managers, Licensed Clinical Social Workers, and other referral sources to inform them of available vacancies.
  • Provide facility tours for potential residents and Case Managers, including hosting lunch as part of the visit.
  • Screen all new referrals to ensure they meet the ODHS Specific Needs Contract Target Group criteria.
  • Verify referral is eligible for Oregon long-term Medicaid and meets all LIHTC requirements.
  • Responsible for scheduling and leading the weekly Admissions Meeting to review and screen resident referrals with the Admissions Team and coordinates nursing and behavioral health assessments.
  • Maintain accurate preadmission records and tracking systems for referrals, determination of outcomes and updating waiting list.
  • Responsible for sending, receiving and tracking required preadmission documentation (e.g. H&P, CAPS, signed Admitting Orders and 494).
  • Coordinate with the Finance Department to ensure completion of all required LIHTC documentation and accurate setup of resident accounts receivable prior to admission.
  • Coordinate with Finance Department to ensure a plan is in place for residents' room & board payments.
  • Confirm with Finance Department if a resident has a representative payee.
  • Responsible for Coordinating Transition Planning prior to move-in to confirm key assignments including scheduling date and time of move-in, identifying furniture, clothing, and other supplies needed.
  • Responsible for providing lease agreement packet and admissions packet for resident's signature on day of move-in.
  • Support coordination of resident transitions, including discharges and transfers, ensuring all required notifications and paperwork are submitted to ODHS.
  • Maintain and track annual renewal of consents, Releases of Information (ROIs), and resident files in compliance with federal and Oregon HIPAA and OAR 411-054 standards.
  • Assist in preparing reports, compliance documentation, and investigative summaries as requested by the Administrator or state representatives.
  • Coordinate with Communications Department to ensure marketing materials are accurate and up to date.
  • Maintain professionalism, confidentiality, and compassion in all interactions with residents, partners, and team members.
  • Additional duties and projects may be assigned as needed.

Administrative and Compliance Support

  • Support Assisted Living Facility leadership in scheduling, calendaring, and tracking project deadlines.
  • Maintain well-organized resident admission records and ensure compliance with all HIPAA, privacy, and documentation standards.
  • Assist the Administrator and Directors in gathering and submitting data for KPI and state-required reporting. Assist with board reporting.
  • Provide administrative support during state surveys, investigations, or internal audits.
  • Additional duties and projects may be assigned as needed.

Skill Profile

The individual in this position is expected to demonstrate the following knowledge, skills, and abilities:

  • Maintains confidentiality of all resident information and strictly follows HIPAA policies and facility privacy protocols.
  • Organizes and prioritizes workload effectively to accomplish assigned responsibilities within established timeframes.
  • Maintains composure and clear judgment during stressful or unexpected situations, adapting readily to changing needs.
  • Understands and applies Oregon Administrative Rules (OARs) and ODHS contract requirements relevant to admissions and behavioral health operations.
  • Demonstrates exceptional organizational skills and consistent attention to detail.

Job Qualifications

The following qualifications are required to perform the essential functions of this position.

  • Education: High school diploma or GED required; Associate or Bachelor's degree preferred.
  • Experience: Minimum two (2) years of experience in healthcare, behavioral health, case management, or admissions coordination.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: Familiarity with Medicaid eligibility requirements and Oregon Assisted Living regulations preferred.
  • Technical Proficiency: Demonstrates advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and the ability to learn new systems, equipment, and best practices to improve workflow and resident care.
  • Communication Skills: Possesses strong written and verbal communication abilities with attention to detail and professionalism.
  • Teamwork: Works independently and collaboratively as part of an interdisciplinary team, maintaining flexibility and cooperation in a dynamic environment.
  • Professional Standards: Demonstrates reliability, punctuality, and adherence to assigned work schedules.
  • Adaptability: Displays the ability and willingness to perform all position responsibilities with competence and initiative.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions listed above.

  • Regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls; and to communicate clearly through talking and hearing.
  • Frequently required to sit for extended periods and to reach with hands and arms.
  • Occasionally required to stand, walk, stoop, kneel, or crouch to perform job-related tasks.
  • Must frequently lift or move objects weighing up to 20 pounds and occasionally lift or move objects up to 25 pounds.
  • Specific vision abilities required include close vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
  • The work environment is typical of a healthcare facility serving individuals with physical and behavioral health needs.
  • Noise level is generally moderate.

Benefits/perks

  • Health insurance (paying 100% of the employee's health premiums, and offering dependent coverage options)
  • Employer Paid Life and Disability Insurance
  • 401(k) option which is available upon 60 days of service and matches employee contribution $1/$1 up to 4%
  • Monthly Tri-Met or parking pass
  • Generous PTO policy
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Meal provided while on site during work shift.

Compensation

Starting Rate - $27 - $29/hour

Schedule

Monday through Friday, 9:00am -5:30pm

About Maybelle Center

Maybelle Center is the Community Health Organization working together with neighbors in downtown Portland to reverse the root causes of social isolation. We promote social health by helping create a sense of belonging with adults facing the stigmas of mental health and financial poverty through our neighborhood programs in affordable housing and assisted living services.

title: Junior Engineer, Bridge Inspection
description:
Popli Design Group (PDG), a growing multi-disciplined Architecture/Engineering firm is seeking a Junior Engineer in the Bridge Inspection Division.


As a Junior Engineer specializing in Bridge Inspection, your role will involve assisting the Bridge Inspection Team Leaders in conducting inspections in the field. You will actively contribute to the inspection process, helping gather data and performing necessary tasks under the guidance of experienced professionals. Additionally, you will be responsible for conducting structural analyses of bridges to determine their capacity, utilizing your engineering knowledge and analytical skills.


The perfect candidate should possess excellent written and verbal communication skills, allowing them to effectively document bridge conditions in the required format. This includes providing clear and concise descriptions along with appropriately referenced photographs. Being focused on providing quality work is essential, demonstrating attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy. You should have a working knowledge of relevant structural concepts pertaining to bridges and other highway structures, enabling you to understand and assess their condition.


Responsibilities

  • Assisting bridge inspection Team Leaders to perform inspections in the field.
  • Structural analyses of bridges to determine the capacity.
  • Entry of data into bridge inspection software and Microsoft Word/Excel/Access; development of structural drawings using CADD, and the compilation of reports and other documents.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document bridge conditions in required format, along with appropriately referenced photographs in a clear and concise manner.
  • Must be focused on providing quality work.
  • Working knowledge of relevant structural concepts of bridges and other highway structures.
  • Experienced in common computer applications (e.g., MS Word, Excel, Access), experience with AutoCAD and/or MicroStation preferred.


Experience

  • Bachelor or master's degree in Civil Engineering.
  • 0-3 years of experience.
  • A Valid Driver's License and acceptable Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) is required.


Work Environment

  • Combination of professional office environment and field work.
  • Work alongside a Professional Engineer (PE).
  • Position includes a career development plan with an established path towards their PE.
  • Field work requires employees to be willing to work in various weather conditions and nature.
  • Required to travel to project sites.


Physical Demands

  • Must physically be able to perform field inspection work, e.g., carry/climb ladders, wade in streams, work around traffic, work at heights, etc.
  • This job requires prolonged periods of sitting at a computer.
  • Lifting up to 50lbs is required.


About Popli Design Group (PDG)


PDG is a well-established multi-disciplinary architecture and engineering firm that has been serving clients since 1982. With four decades of experience and expertise, we have evolved from a transportation engineering firm to a comprehensive, full-service organization with seven office locations in New York State. Our extensive portfolio of successful projects has earned us a trusted reputation among our clients.

title: Fabrication Production Planner
description:
Fouts Bros Inc. is a family-owned business since 1952 with facilities in Georgia and Texas. Fouts Bros Inc. is proud to have become one of the largest and most diverse commercial truck manufacturers in the US. Fouts Bros Inc. is committed to developing new commercial vehicles that provide industry-best value, quality, and dependability.


Our company's core values are quality, efficiency, continuous improvement, safety, and teamwork. We believe in conducting business with honesty and transparency, continuously seeking new ways to improve and evolve, fostering relationships with our community and supporting local initiatives, and operating in an environmentally responsible manner to minimize our impact on the planet.


Job Summary:

The Fabrication Production Planner is responsible for creating, scheduling, monitoring, and closing internal fabricated production orders for the FAB shop using Microsoft Dynamics AX. This position also purchases required raw materials from outside vendors to support FAB production needs. The role ensures fabricated components and required materials are planned, ordered, and produced in alignment with sales order shipment requirements, available capacity, material readiness, and internal production priorities. The planner serves as the link between sales order demand, supplier material availability, shop floor execution, inventory consumption, and production order completion.


Key Responsibilities:

· Review sales order shipment needs and determine required fabricated components, quantities, and due dates.

· Create internal FAB production orders in Microsoft Dynamics AX based on sales order demand, inventory requirements, and approved fabrication priorities.

· Plan and maintain the FAB shop production schedule to support customer shipment commitments and internal operational needs.

· Coordinate with sales, purchasing, inventory, warehouse, and production teams to confirm material availability, capacity, and schedule feasibility.

· Purchase required raw materials from outside vendors to support FAB production schedules, sales order shipment needs, and inventory requirements.

· Coordinate with outside vendors on raw material pricing, lead times, order placement, delivery status, and shortage resolution.

· Monitor open FAB production orders to ensure they are released, started, completed, and closed in a timely manner.

· Update production order dates, quantities, statuses, and related planning information in Microsoft Dynamics AX as priorities or shipment requirements change.

· Communicate schedule changes, shortages, delays, and risks that may impact sales order shipment timing.

· Demonstrated vendor negotiation skills, including the ability to evaluate pricing, lead times, delivery commitments, and supplier performance while supporting cost, quality, and schedule objectives.

· Working knowledge of production orders, bills of material, inventory transactions, and manufacturing workflows.

· Experience using Microsoft Dynamics AX or similar ERP system preferred.

· Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and ERP-based data entry.

· Ability to read and interpret sales order requirements, part numbers, due dates, and production priorities.

· Strong attention to detail, including the ability to accurately enter and verify item numbers, quantities, due dates, vendor information, production order statuses, material consumption, and inventory transactions.

· Strong communication skills, including the ability to interact professionally with outside vendors regarding pricing, lead times, order status, delivery issues, shortages, and problem resolution.

· Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to investigate production order discrepancies, vendor delays, material shortages, scheduling conflicts, and inventory transaction issues through to resolution.

· Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize multiple production orders, purchase orders, vendor follow-ups, deadlines, schedule changes, and competing operational priorities.

Key Competencies:

· Production planning and schedule management

· ERP transaction accuracy

· Inventory and material consumption awareness

· Raw material purchasing and supplier coordination

· Vendor negotiation and cost-conscious purchasing decisions

· Problem solving, root-cause analysis, and discrepancy resolution

· Professional communication with vendors, production teams, purchasing, sales, inventory, and warehouse personnel

· Sense of urgency and follow-through

· Detail-oriented documentation and recordkeeping

· Highly organized work habits, including proactive follow-up, schedule tracking, document control, and timely completion of planning and purchasing tasks.


Attributes:

· High school diploma or equivalent required; associate degree in business, supply chain, manufacturing, or related field preferred.

· Experience in production planning, scheduling, inventory control, manufacturing coordination, or a related operational role.

· Experience with purchasing, vendor communication, raw material planning, or procurement support preferred.

title: Senior Designer, Events
description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

  • Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.
  • What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.
  • It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

YOUR MISSION

The Senior Designer, Experiential owns the creative development and direction of True Anomaly’s events experiences.

You develop experiential concepts and creative direction that make complex technology tangible and create a clear, memorable experience of the company. Working from creative and business strategy, you define how True Anomaly shows up physically at events; the spatial form, narrative journey, and environmental expression.

For assigned work, you define the concept, narrative, user journey, visual language and environmental expression, then maintain that creative direction through install and event launch.

Our Principal, Experiential & Environmental Design owns the broader vision and standards for True Anomaly’s physical expression. You work closely with them and apply and extend that overarching direction within events, partnering with Creative Strategy and Business Development on where and why the company should show up, and with production teams that own the operational planning and delivery.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Event Strategy and Creative Partnership

  • Partner with Marketing and Creative Strategy to understand the strategic intent behind events: why it matters, who it must reach, and what the audience should believe or feel. Advise on how experiential format and investment level can best serve those objectives.
  • Collaborate with Business Development, Recruiting, and Creative Strategy to pressure-test event opportunities and advise on feasibility, format, and creative approach before concept work begins.

Event Concepting & Creative Development

  • Develop creative concepts for events and experiential programs, translating strategic intent into spatial and experiential form, from initial idea through final creative direction.
  • Define the narrative, user journey, key moments, visual language, spatial expression, and emotional arc of each experience.
  • Develop and present concepts, references, sketches, experience frameworks, and recommendations to internal partners and senior leadership.
  • Lead creative development across graphic and spatial design, content, motion, interactive elements, demonstrations, branded objects, and environmental details as appropriate.
  • Ensure each concept is distinctive to True Anomaly, appropriate to its audience, and grounded in the company's brand strategy and mission.

Design Development, Spaces, and Systems

  • Direct internal teams, agencies, fabricators, and production partners through design development; create and review layouts, renderings, drawings, prototypes, materials, graphics, content, and environmental elements.
  • Partner with the Events & Styling Lead on furniture, finishes, materials, rentals, styling, and final environmental details.
  • Develop repeatable kits of parts, modular experience systems, and event-specific standards that allow the company to move quickly without making every experience feel identical.
  • Shape demo rooms and partner with Facilities on spaces that must support hosted events, media moments, recordings, demonstrations, talent programs, and other marketing objectives.
  • Review work with leadership at key milestones and maintain the creative through-line from concept through fabrication, installation, and live experience.

Production Partnership

  • Build and maintain a trusted network of agencies, designers, fabricators, craftspeople, rental partners, and special vendors that balance creative ambition, executional quality and responsible investment for each project.
  • Partner with the Event Producer(s) and/or external production lead from the earliest concept stage so ideas can be delivered on time, within budget, and in keeping with the design intent.
  • Design within established budget and schedule parameters. Advise on budget implications of creative decisions, flag scope-versus-budget mismatches early, and recommend creative tradeoffs when budget or schedule constraints require adjustment.
  • Provide timely creative decisions, drawing and prototype reviews, approvals, references, content, and specifications needed for production to advance.
  • Participate in site visits, production reviews, and key vendor conversations; be on site for priority installations and events to direct creative quality and resolve design questions.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree and 8-11 years of experience developing creative concepts and directing brand events, experiential activations, conferences, demonstrations, executive gatherings, or other live experiences; or Master's degree and 6 years of relevant experience.
  • Portfolio demonstrating strong experiential concepting, creative direction, narrative thinking, and final executed work.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business, audience, and brand strategy into distinctive physical experiences.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary creative teams and directing agencies, designers, fabricators, content partners, and production specialists.
  • Strong understanding of spatial experience, user journey, graphics, materials, objects, content, technology, and live moments.
  • Comfort working hands-on across concepting, design development, vendor creative direction, and on-site execution. This is a player-coach role: you'll both direct external partners and execute design work yourself as the project demands.
  • Deep knowledge of event production, fabrication, AV, logistics, installation, and venue constraints sufficient to make responsible creative decisions.
  • Ability to develop creative work within defined budgets and schedules and to make sound tradeoffs without losing the central idea.
  • Excellent presentation, communication, collaboration, and stakeholder-management skills, with calm judgment when conditions change.
  • Willingness to travel and work outside conventional hours when required by an installation or live
  • Experience in technology, aerospace, defense, automotive, industrial design, or another technically complex category is helpful but not required.
  • Genuine interest in aerospace, defense, or national security is a meaningful signal. Domain expertise is not required; intellectual seriousness about the mission is.

COMPENSATION

  • Base Salary: $130,000 - $235,000
  • Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Work Location—Successful candidates will be located near Long Beach, CA. While we observe a hybrid work environment, some work must be done on site.

This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below. #LI-Hybrid

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

True Anomaly is committed to equal employment opportunity on any basis protected by applicable state and federal laws. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us.

title: Senior Laser Technical Specialist
description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Manufacturing team owns all process development, fabrication strategy, and production equipment for Terran R, our next generation, reusable rocket. This team has a wide variety of responsibilities – from factory floor layout, to developing complex tooling for novel processes, and interfacing with our vehicle engineering team to heavily influence design of the rocket. We leverage our deep expertise to translate engineering requirements into highly optimized production lines, working cross functionally to consistently enhance the vehicle program.

About the Role:

  • 8+ years of professional experience working with laser trackers
  • Experience analyzing data and generating data reports
  • 8+ Experience with Verisurf X
  • Experience using inspection equipment, such as, micrometers, gauge blocks, dial indicators, height gauges, optical comparators, profilometers, CMM and laser trackers
  • Use in-depth familiarity of GD&T to interpret blueprints at all assembly levels
  • Collect geometric data via laser tracker through model-based software such as Verisurf
  • Discern how best to establish a reference system for the current task then apply it and install it both on and off the part
  • Provide analysis of collected data and evaluate it to provide direction for remaining operations
  • Integrate process monitoring with the fabrication process to locate both welding details and machining details

About You:

  • Understanding of the manufacturing process of large structures from concept to completion
  • Ability to precision locate machine details in extreme environments
  • Strong mechanical aptitude
  • Ability to visualize 3D space and integrate complex geometries on to both large and small fabrications

Nice to haves but not required:

  • Ability to maintain the highest level of safety on the job site and bring new ideas of how to continue to work safely and effectively in new locations and changing environments

## Logistics Specialist

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems

Poway

California

Job Summary

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), an affiliate of General Atomics, is a world leader in proven, reliable remotely piloted aircraft and tactical reconnaissance radars, as well as advanced high-resolution surveillance systems.

Under general direction with limited review, this position plans, administers, and continuously improves integrated logistics strategies, processes, and tools. The role ensures customer support requirements and objectives are achieved within budget and on schedule while aligning maintenance execution, aircraft status, and logistics demand across all operating sites. The position coordinates with site maintenance, engineering, field operations, logistics, and customer organizations to support aircraft availability, timely spares fulfillment, accurate demand planning, and effective product support. The role also analyzes operational and supply data, documents findings, communicates recommendations, and develops logistics processes that address business and customer needs.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Plans and administers integrated logistics strategies, processes, tools, and related support activities in accordance with program, customer, and business requirements.
- Ensures customer support requirements and objectives are achieved within established budget, schedule, performance, and contractual parameters.
- Aligns maintenance execution, aircraft status, and logistics demand across all operating sites by reviewing daily status reports and coordinating priorities.
- Supports scheduled and unscheduled maintenance, aircraft modifications, and service bulletin implementation by coordinating required materials, resources, and logistics activities.
- Monitors aircraft reliability, availability, and downtime; evaluates logistics-related impacts and supports corrective actions to improve operational performance.
- Manages and prioritizes Mission Capable Supply (MICAP) requests based on mission impact, operational urgency, aircraft status, and available resources.
- Coordinates with maintenance, engineering, field operations, logistics, and customer teams to ensure timely spares fulfillment, accurate demand planning, and resolution of supply issues.
- Analyzes part usage, demand, aircraft status, and related data to determine warehouse stocking requirements, improve inventory positioning, and support replenishment planning.
- Reviews service bulletins and technical requirements to support part allocation, material planning, supply decisions, and implementation activities.
- Continuously improves standard logistics processes, including supportability analysis planning, logistics database development, product support and replenishment systems, product support data interchange systems, demand management, and related functions.
- Develops and implements logistics processes, tools, and procedures based on customer requirements, business needs, operational demand, and lessons learned.
- Build and maintain customer relationships through logistics initiatives and support activities.
- Integrates knowledge gained from customers, competitors, other industries, industry groups, and professional training to improve logistics capabilities and the Company’s competitive position.
- Identifies logistics issues and develop solutions to complex problems, including resource reallocation, process improvements, and modifications to manufacturing or supply chain activities.
- Documents analyses, findings, recommendations, and results; communicates information to technical staff and management; and delivers presentations as required.
- Participates in planning and review sessions addressing cost, schedule, technical performance, customer support, aircraft status, and logistics requirements.
- Ensures that all applicable laws, regulations, contractual requirements, Company policies, and other obligations are observed wherever and whenever business is conducted on behalf of the Company.
- Ensure that work is accomplished safely and in accordance with established operating procedures and practices.
- Additional Functions: Other duties as assigned or required.

We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals with diverse backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply.

Job Qualifications

- Typically requires a bachelor's degree and six or more years of progressive logistics management experience. May substitute equivalent experience in lieu of education.
- Knowledge of integrated logistics, product support, supply chain management, aircraft maintenance support, or related discipline.
- Understanding supportability analysis, demand management, replenishment planning, inventory management, and logistics data systems.
- Ability to analyze aircraft, maintenance, part, inventory, and demand data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
- Ability to prioritize competing requirements based on mission impact, customer needs, cost, schedule, and operational risk.
- Strong communication, technical writing, presentation, coordination, and relationship-building skills.
- Ability to work effectively with customers, maintenance personnel, engineers, field operations, logistics organizations, and management.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities with limited review and general direction.
- Proficiency with standard business, logistics, and data-analysis tools.
- May lead a team of professional employees on assigned aspects of project(s).
- Able to work extended hours and travel as required.
- Ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Security Clearance is required.

title: Sr. Strategic Sourcing Analyst

Docusign brings agreements to life. Over 1.5 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. Our organization is seeking a detail-oriented and analytically-minded Strategic Sourcing Analyst to join our procurement team. In this role, you will support the execution of sourcing strategies, manage supplier engagement, and drive operational excellence across General and Administrative (G and A) and other indirect categories. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to execute competitive procurement events, negotiate contracts, and maintain strong supplier relationships that deliver value and mitigate risk.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Director, Strategic Sourcing.

Responsibility

  • Execute sourcing strategies and competitive procurement events (RFP, RFI, RFQ) across multiple G and A and indirect categories, including office services, facilities, consulting, HR services, and professional services
  • Lead intake, scoping, and requirements definition for sourcing initiatives using modern procurement orchestration tools (ZipHQ, Levelpath, or equivalent) to ensure structured, repeatable processes
  • Negotiate terms, pricing, and key business clauses in agreements (MSAs, SOWs, order forms); use AI tools strategically to analyze contracts and surface risk, while applying your own judgment to business implications
  • Support supplier onboarding, risk assessments, and compliance activities in collaboration with Legal, Information Security, Finance, and Third Party Governance teams
  • Manage contract lifecycle activities: track renewals, monitor expirations, identify renewal opportunities, and maintain accurate contract and supplier documentation
  • Analyze spend data, prepare reports, and create dashboards to provide cost visibility and identify savings opportunities; supplement analysis with AI insights while maintaining critical evaluation of output
  • Identify and recommend process improvements to enhance sourcing workflows, reduce cycle time, and strengthen supplier management practices
  • Maintain systems-level thinking when evaluating category opportunities; understand how sourcing decisions impact downstream procurement operations and organizational objectives

Hybrid: Employee divides their time between in-office and remote work. Access to an office location is required. (Frequency: Minimum 2 days per week; may vary by team but will be weekly in-office expectation)

Preferred job designations are not guaranteed when changing positions within Docusign. Docusign reserves the right to change a position's job designation depending on business needs and as permitted by local law.


What you bring

  • BA or BS degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Finance, or related field
  • Experience leading or supporting sourcing events (RFPs, RFIs, RFQs) with structured intake and stakeholder alignment
  • Experience with contract structures, procurement documents (MSAS, SOWS, NDAs), and standard business terms
  • Experience with Excel, Google Workspace, and data analysis fundamentals

  • Experience with P2P and sourcing systems (Oracle, Workday Scout, Coupa)

  • Process and systems mindset: ability to design workflows, think in terms of end-to-end processes, and identify inefficiencies
  • Excellent attention to detail, communication skills, and ability to manage competing priorities in a deadline-driven environment

Life at Docusign



Working here

Docusign is committed to building trust and making the world more agreeable for our employees, customers and the communities in which we live and work. You can count on us to listen, be honest, and try our best to do what’s right, every day. At Docusign, everything is equal.

Operating in compliance with State of New Jersey substance use treatment standards and aligned with the mission of Good News Home, this position integrates Christian principles and biblical scripture into every aspect of client care to build a strong spiritual foundation for long-term recovery.

  • Family Support & Life Skills: Engage with family members to provide recovery education and community resources. Assist residents with developing practical coping strategies, personal budgeting, and life skills (including guided personal shopping).

title: Senior Software Engineer II
description:
Optum is a global organization that delivers care, aided by technology to help millions of people live healthier lives. The work you do with our team will directly improve health outcomes by connecting people with the care, pharmacy benefits, data and resources they need to feel their best. Here, you will find a culture guided by inclusion, talented peers, comprehensive benefits and career development opportunities. Come make an impact on the communities we serve as you help us advance health optimization on a global scale. Join us to start Caring. Connecting. Growing together.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Understand business requirements, application architecture, and enterprise systems to design and deliver scalable, high-quality solutions
  • Lead the design, development, testing, deployment, and maintenance of enterprise applications using Trizetto Facets, SQL, Python, Java, or equivalent technologies
  • Provide technical leadership and guidance to engineering teams, promoting best practices in software development, code quality, and system design
  • Drive architecture discussions and contribute to the design of scalable, secure, resilient, and maintainable applications
  • Develop clean, reusable, and maintainable code while establishing coding standards and engineering best practices
  • Design, optimize, and troubleshoot complex SQL queries, database objects, and data access layers to support business-critical applications
  • Design and develop RESTful APIs, microservices, and integration solutions across enterprise platforms
  • Collaborate with architects, product owners, business stakeholders, and cross-functional teams to define technical solutions aligned with business objectives
  • Lead cloud adoption initiatives and support the deployment, monitoring, scalability, and operational excellence of applications in cloud environments
  • Design, implement, and enhance CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps or similar platforms
  • Champion DevOps practices including source control management, automated testing, release management, infrastructure automation, and continuous delivery
  • Evaluate and leverage AI/ML and Generative AI technologies to improve engineering productivity, business processes, and customer outcomes
  • Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through technical coaching, code reviews, design reviews, and knowledge-sharing initiatives
  • Ensure adherence to security, compliance, performance, and reliability standards throughout the software development lifecycle
  • Lead production support activities, perform root cause analysis, and implement preventive measures to improve system stability and performance
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on engineering excellence, automation, operational efficiency, and innovation
  • Communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, providing regular updates on technical solutions, risks, and project status
  • Demonstrate ownership and accountability for end-to-end delivery of strategic technology solutions
  • Comply with the terms and conditions of the employment contract, company policies and procedures, and any and all directives (such as, but not limited to, transfer and/or re-assignment to different work locations, change in teams and/or work shifts, policies in regards to flexibility of work benefits and/or work environment, alternative work arrangements, and other decisions that may arise due to the changing business environment). The Company may adopt, vary or rescind these policies and directives in its absolute discretion and without any limitation (implied or otherwise) on its ability to do so

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, MCA, or equivalent
  • 12+ years of experience in software design, development, and delivery of enterprise applications
  • Solid hands-on experience with Trizetto Facets, SQL, Python, Java, or equivalent programming languages and frameworks
  • Proven experience designing and developing scalable, maintainable, and secure enterprise-grade software solutions
  • Solid experience designing and implementing RESTful APIs, microservices, and distributed systems
  • Experience working with cloud platforms and cloud-native application architectures
  • Hands-on experience implementing and managing CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Jenkins, or equivalent technologies
  • Experience leading technical initiatives and influencing architectural and engineering decisions
  • Deep expertise in SQL, including performance optimization, database design, data modeling, and troubleshooting
  • Exposure to AI/ML concepts, Generative AI, LLMs, intelligent automation, or AI-assisted software development
  • Solid understanding of software architecture, object-oriented design principles, design patterns, and application security best practices
  • Solid understanding of Agile, Scrum, and modern SDLC methodologies
  • Solid proficiency with Git-based source control and modern software development practices
  • Proven excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills
  • Proven solid stakeholder management, collaboration, and communication skills
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers and drive technical excellence across teams

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Azure, AI, Cloud, DevOps, or Architecture-related certifications
  • Experience integrating AI/ML solutions using frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn, LangChain, Azure AI Studio, or similar platforms
  • Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, container orchestration, and cloud-native application development
  • Experience designing and implementing scalable microservices-based architectures
  • Healthcare and Trizetto Facets domain experience
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and delivering large-scale enterprise transformation programs
  • Familiarity with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools and DevOps automation practices

At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and make the health system work better for everyone. We believe everyone-of every race, gender, sexuality, age, location and income-deserves the opportunity to live their healthiest life.
