Licenses Required

  • Current RQI Healthcare Provider eCredential through the University of Utah Health RQI system. The eCredential is to be obtained within 30 days of hire.
* Additional license requirements as determined by the hiring department.

Qualifications (Preferred)

Working Conditions and Physical Demands

Employee must be able to meet the following requirements with or without an accommodation.

  • This position involves intensive work that may exert up to 50 pounds and may consistently require lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling or otherwise moving objects, such as medical equipment, or patients while providing care in a psychiatric setting. Workers in this position may be exposed to infectious diseases.

Physical Requirements

Carrying, Lifting, Listening, Manual Dexterity, Pulling and/or Pushing, Reaching, Sitting, Speaking, Standing, Stooping and Crouching, Walking

title: AI Evaluation Methodology Lead
description:
Do you want to define the evaluation methodology and technical requirements that underpin effective AI evaluation and monitoring within the business at one of the leading financial institutions in the Nordics?
Join Danske Bank's newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management. As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will hold a 1st Line of Defence role with clear ownership of the technical methodologies used to evaluate AI models and AI-enabled solutions, and of the technical requirements for the platforms that support their evaluation and ongoing monitoring. You will translate business-owned risk and control needs into clear methods, metrics, data, evidence, traceability and platform capabilities that can be implemented consistently across the Bank's technology landscape.
This is a unique opportunity to shape a consistent, scalable and evidence-based capability through which the business identifies, evaluates, monitors and manages AI model risk.

This role can be based in Copenhagen, Denmark, Vilnius, Lithuania, Warsaw, Poland, Stockholm, Sweden or Helsinki, Finland.

What you will be doing
The AI Model Assessment team is a business-owned control capability that performs evidence-based assessments of AI models and AI-enabled solutions across the Bank. We work with business owners, developers, engineers and platform teams to understand how solutions operate, define the evidence required for assessment, and establish the evaluation and monitoring capabilities needed to identify, assess and manage model risk where it arises.
Our mission is to enable responsible innovation by providing the business with a consistent and scalable framework for evaluating AI systems, monitoring their performance and risk, and demonstrating that appropriate controls are operating effectively.

As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will own the evaluation methodology and define the technical requirements for the platforms, tooling and data capabilities used by the 1st Line of Defence to evaluate and monitor AI models and AI-enabled solutions. Your mandate is to ensure that the business has robust, implementable and auditable means to assess its AI risks and controls. Your focus will be on specifying what the evaluation and monitoring capability must deliver rather than owning software development or platform operations.

You will work closely with the independent 2nd Line AI model risk function, which sets the overarching risk framework and provides oversight and constructive challenge. You will translate that framework into practical evaluation methodologies, technical requirements and business-owned controls, provide transparent evidence of how requirements are implemented, and support the resolution of identified gaps.

Your responsibilities will include:
• Owning, developing and maintaining the methodology for evaluating AI models and AI-enabled solutions, including evaluation objectives, test approaches, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.
• Defining the functional and technical requirements for evaluation and monitoring platforms that enable risk management, including data ingestion, test execution, metric calculation, observability, evidence capture, reporting, access controls and auditability.
• Translating model risk, business and assessment requirements into reusable evaluation methods, representative datasets, metrics, thresholds, monitoring indicators and structured evidence requirements.
• Determining how AI system architectures, components, dependencies and data flows affect evaluation scope, test design, monitoring coverage and the technical capabilities required from supporting platforms.
• Defining platform-agnostic requirements that support evaluation and monitoring across environments such as AWS Bedrock and AgentCore, Databricks, Azure OpenAI and embedded third-party AI platforms.
• Setting requirements for reproducibility and end-to-end traceability across models, prompts, datasets, configurations, system components, evaluation results, monitoring signals and changes over time.
• Prioritising opportunities to standardise and automate evaluation and monitoring activities, and working with evaluators, platform owners and engineers to convert approved control requirements into practical platform capabilities.
• Engaging with the Second Line model risk function to interpret applicable requirements, demonstrate how they are operationalised, respond to constructive challenge, and ensure that evaluation and monitoring evidence supports effective independent oversight.

About you
An experienced AI evaluation, model risk, data, architecture or platform professional who can establish rigorous evaluation methodologies and turn business risk and control needs into clear, implementable technical requirements for enterprise platforms and tooling.

You have:
• Proven experience designing or governing AI/ML evaluation methodologies, including test objectives, datasets, metrics, thresholds, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.
• Experience translating evaluation, monitoring, risk and control needs into functional and technical requirements for platforms, tooling, data pipelines and reporting capabilities.
• Experience with AI/ML evaluation, business-owned model risk management and controls, technical assurance, MLOps, LLMOps, AI platforms or AI observability.
• Familiarity with cloud AI services or enterprise AI platforms; experience with AWS Bedrock or AgentCore, Databricks or Mosaic AI, Azure OpenAI, or comparable platforms is an advantage.
• Strong understanding of evaluation and monitoring principles, including representative datasets, experiment configuration, metric design, regression testing, monitoring indicators, traceability and evidence capture.
• Ability to distinguish methodology and requirements ownership from platform implementation, while collaborating effectively with engineers and platform owners. Python or similar tools for analysis, prototyping or investigation are an advantage, but software development is not the primary focus of the role.
• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to articulate evaluation, monitoring, risk and control requirements across business, assessment, platform, engineering, architecture, data and risk functions.
Experience with AI evaluation or observability technologies, for example Phoenix or comparable tools, is an advantage but is not a prerequisite.

What we offer you
You will join the newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management, helping build the Bank's consistent and scalable business-owned capability for AI evaluation, monitoring and model risk management.
The team combines technical AI evaluation expertise with model risk management and works across the Bank's AI initiatives. In this role, you will connect evaluators with platform, engineering, architecture and data teams by defining the methods and technical requirements their solutions must support, ensuring that risk ownership and control evidence remain anchored in the business.

If hired in Lithuania, your monthly salary would range from 4320 EUR to 6480 EUR gross (based on your competencies relevant for the job).
Additionally, each Danske Bank employee receives employee benefits package which includes:
• Growth opportunities: professional & supportive team, e-learnings, numerous development programs; (incl. professional certificates); 100+ professions for internal mobility opportunities.
• Health & Well-being: a diverse, inclusive, work & life balance work environment; additional health insurance; mental well-being practices; partial psychologist counselling compensation; silence and sleep zones at the office; game rooms.
• Hybrid working conditions: Work from home up to two days a week; home office budget (after the probation period); modern Danske Campus workplace developed with anthropologist for the best employee experience.
• Additional days of leave: for rest, health, volunteering, exams in higher education institutions, and other important activities. Moreover, for seniority with Danske Bank.
• Monetary compensation package: accidents & critical diseases insurance; financial support in case of unfortunate events, travel insurance; IIIrd Pillar Pension Fund contribution.
See all the benefits HERE.

Your job function (position) in the job contract will be AI Science

Are you ready for the next step?
If you are passionate about defining robust AI evaluation methodologies and the technical requirements for scalable evaluation and monitoring platforms that support effective business ownership of AI risk, we would love to hear from you.
For questions about the role, please contact Khaled Alizai, Head of AI Model Assessment at khali@danskebank.dk. We are screening the applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply.
Join us and help build the business-owned foundation for effective AI model evaluation, monitoring and risk management at Danske Bank.

title: Surgical First Assist/Surgical Tech
description:
Surgical Technologist / First Assist

The Surgical Technologist / First Assist is responsible for supporting the surgical team before, during, and after operative procedures. This position performs surgical technologist duties while also providing first-assist support to the surgeon within the individual’s education, training, certification, and scope of practice. The Surgical Technologist / First Assist helps maintain a safe, efficient surgical environment and ensures appropriate instrumentation, supplies, and equipment are available throughout each procedure.


Primary Responsibilities:

  1. Support the mission, vision, and values of the organization.
  2. Prepare the operating room for surgical procedures, including equipment, instruments, supplies, and sterile field setup.
  3. Review physician preference cards and ensure appropriate instruments, supplies, implants, and equipment are available for scheduled procedures.
  4. Maintain sterile technique and follow infection prevention practices throughout surgical procedures.
  5. Perform surgical counts in collaboration with the circulating RN according to facility policy.
  6. Anticipate the needs of the surgeon and surgical team by passing instruments, supplies, and equipment efficiently throughout the procedure.
  7. Assist with patient positioning, skin preparation, draping, and other perioperative activities within scope of practice.
  8. Provide first-assist support to the surgeon as permitted by training, certification, facility policy, and applicable regulations.
  9. Perform first-assist functions as appropriate, including providing exposure, retraction, hemostasis, tissue handling, and assistance with wound closure under the direction of the surgeon.
  10. Assist with application of dressings and other post-procedure activities as directed.
  11. Handle surgical specimens appropriately and according to facility policy.
  12. Assist with room turnover and preparation for subsequent surgical cases.
  13. Inspect instruments and equipment for proper function and communicate any concerns or needed repairs.
  14. Collaborate professionally with surgeons, anesthesia providers, nurses, sterile processing staff, and other members of the perioperative team.
  15. Follow organizational policies, regulatory and accreditation standards, and applicable professional guidelines.
  16. Participate in quality improvement and patient safety initiatives.
  17. Maintain patient privacy and confidentiality at all times.

title: Whatcom Early Learning Program Manager
description:

Interested in making a difference in your community while building a career? Join our team as the Whatcom Early Learning Program Manager!

WHO WE ARE:

For 60 years, Opportunity Council has worked throughout Northwest Washington to build just, equitable communities through service, investment, and collaboration. Part of a national network of Community Action Agencies, we are dedicated to helping people help each other and themselves—building a community where everyone has the chance to thrive and contribute.

The Whatcom Early Leaning Programs Manager WELP oversees the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of classroom-based services for children one to five years of age, with comprehensive wrap-around services for all enrolled children for medical, dental, behavioral and specialized education services. The WELP Manager works with service area coordinators to ensure services are carried out in accordance with EHS center-based/Head Start/ECEAP Performance Standards, as well as local, state and federal regulations, service area work plans, and program policies and procedures. In collaboration with other Early Learning & Family Services personnel, the PS Manager tracks and reports on program and performance outcomes for governance bodies and funders.

  • Provides direct supervision and support to Health coordinator, subcontracting Liaisons and Site/Center Supervisors.
  • Participates as a member of ELAFS Leadership Team.
  • Provides on-going training and professional development for staff.
  • Participates in community needs assessment processes within Opportunity Council and in the community at large.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

  • Bachelors or advanced degree in Early Childhood Education/Child Development/Human Services or related field (advanced degree preferred) or relevant education/experience.
  • Minimum five years relevant experience working with similarly aged children and their families in an educational or social service setting.
  • Minimum three years supervisory and management experience, with specific training in supervisory skills, communications, group process, observation techniques, basic financial management and grant management.
  • Appropriate training or experience in social services, particularly work with low-income households.
  • Basic knowledge of operations of early childhood development programs (Head Start or ECEAP.)
  • Have (or obtain prior to hire date) and maintain Washington State Food Handler’s Permit during length of employment.
  • Valid Washington State driver’s license and five-year driving history within Opportunity Council’s Auto Insurance Standards.
  • Initial health examination indicating you are fit for duty and free from communicable disease within 60 days of hire. Medical check-ups are required every two years thereafter.
  • Completed TB test prior to hire date.
  • Proof of MMR Vaccination Status.
  • Criminal records check and obtain a Washington Portable Background clearance to ascertain that the applicant has not been convicted of a child abuse or neglect offense per Washington State Child Abuse Law (Ch. 486, Laws of 1987) or DSHS licensing requirements.
  • Current First Aid card and Infant/Child CPR training (or obtain within 30 days), and must maintain current certificates for length of employment.
  • Must have Bloodborne Pathogens/HIV/AIDS training (or obtain within 60 days).

We place a strong value in hiring individuals with lived experiences of, poverty and/or homelessness or who have previously participated in Opportunity Council programs or other social services.

OUR BENEFITS PACKAGE:

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance.

  • HSA and FSA plans, subject to plan terms

ABOUT WHATCOM COUNTY:

Working with Opportunity Council in Whatcom County is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something bigger. Surrounded by the natural beauty of the Pacific Northwest, our community is rooted in compassion, collaboration, and a shared commitment to positive change. Whether you're supporting local families, advocating for equity, or building programs that uplift our neighbors, you'll find purpose and connection here. Join us in building a stronger Whatcom County where everyone has the chance to thrive and contribute

We believe our team should reflect the communities we serve. That’s why we strongly encourage people of color, LGBTQIA+ individuals, Veterans, and people with disabilities to apply. title: Senior Program Coordinator, Executive Customer Engagement
description:

title: Software Engineer
description:
Job Description

Job Description

Software Engineer, AI-Accelerated Development

You're already reaching for AI tools before you write a line of code. What if your next team was built entirely around that instinct?

About the Company:

Our client is a cloud communications API platform (CPaaS) powering voice and text messaging for more than 1,500 companies, from contact centers to fintech platforms to mobile carriers. Their platform includes voice APIs, SMS/MMS messaging, RCS for Business, branded calling solutions, and bring-your-own-carrier (BYOC) options, all built on carrier redundancy, compliance, and U.S.-based support. When a call or text absolutely has to go through, their customers count on this team to make it happen.

The Opportunity:

We are looking for a software engineer who's already comfortable working alongside AI tools day to day and wants to build that fluency further inside a small, senior engineering team. You'll work across their Voice, Messaging, and Platform Services stack, using AI coding assistants for scaffolding, code review, test generation, debugging, and documentation, while sharpening your own judgment about when to trust the output and when to override it. This is a great fit for someone early in their AI-assisted development journey who wants to grow into it quickly, surrounded by people who've already been doing this daily.

What You'll Actually Do:

  • Design, build, and ship features across Voice, Messaging, and Platform Services systems (APIs, routing logic, carrier integrations, messaging pipelines)
  • Use AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or similar) as part of your daily workflow
  • Start experimenting with AI agents for real engineering tasks (testing, documentation upkeep, code migration) under guidance from more senior teammates
  • Support production systems handling real-time voice and messaging traffic, including a weekly on-call rotation
  • Work closely with product management on scoping and estimation
  • Write clear documentation, including notes on what worked and didn't with AI-assisted workflows

What You Bring:
  • 3 to 5 years of professional software engineering experience, ideally including backend/API work or distributed systems

title: Logistics Coordinator - Reverse Logistics, Fredericia, Carlsberg Danmark
description:
Vil du være med til at sikre, at millioner af flasker, fustager og paller finder den rette vej tilbage i Carlsbergs værdikæde?

Carlsberg Danmark leder efter en Logistics Coordinator til Admin-teamet i Fredericia med fokus på overblik og forbedringer. Her får du en central rolle med ansvar for at skabe overblik, optimere processer og sikre et effektivt flow af returemballage, paller og kvartpaller på tværs af vores forsyningskæde.

Hvis du motiveres af data, drift, samarbejde og løbende forbedringer, kan dette være dit næste karriereskridt.

En nøgleposition i vores supply chain.

Som Logistics Coordinator – Reverse Logistics bliver du en vigtig del af teamet i Admin & Process Development. Du får ejerskab for vores reverse logistics-processer og spiller en central rolle i at sikre transparens, omkostningskontrol og høj operationel performance.

Du vil få en central rolle som go-to person inden for palle- og returlogistik og samarbejde tæt med kolleger på tværs af lager, distribution, produktion, planlægning, controlling, procurement og customer supply.

Dine primære ansvarsområder

Du kommer blandt andet til at:

  • Sikre kontrol over pallebeholdninger, returstrømme, kvalitet og tab
  • Identificere og håndtere afvigelser mellem forbrug, modtagelser og afregninger
  • Sikre tilgængelighed af paller gennem løbende planlægning og opfølgning
  • Skabe gennemsigtighed i data og performance gennem analyser og rapportering
  • Sikre korrekt økonomisk afregning af returstrømme
  • Understøtte månedsafslutning med opfølgning, afstemninger og datakvalitet
  • Identificere og gennemføre forbedringer i processer og arbejdsgange inden for reverse logistics
  • Bidrage til en sikker, struktureret og effektiv logistisk drift

Hvem er du?

Vi forestiller os, at du har en relevant uddannelse inden for logistik, supply chain eller værdikædeledelse og et par års erfaring fra en lignende rolle.

Derudover ser vi gerne, at du:

  • Er god til at arbejde metodisk og trives med en datadrevet arbejdsform
  • Har en struktureret og systematisk tilgang til dit arbejde
  • Har erfaring med reverse logistics og gerne kendskab til palleflow i en produktions- eller logistikvirksomhed
  • Tager ansvar og følger opgaver helt til dørs
  • Er nysgerrig på forbedringer og ser muligheder frem for begrænsninger
  • Kan samarbejde på tværs af organisationen og skabe gode relationer
  • Kommunikerer klart og professionelt på både dansk og engelsk

Kendskab til Lean er en fordel, men ikke et krav.

At arbejde hos Carlsberg Danmark

Hos Carlsberg Danmark bidrager du til udviklingen af nogle af landets mest kendte brands – Carlsberg, Tuborg, Somersby og Coca-Cola – som vi leverer til mere end 10.000 kunder. Vi viderefører Carlsbergs arv og forener den med en moderne, fremadskuende tilgang. Vores fælles mål “Brewing for a better today and tomorrow” gennemsyrer alt, hvad vi gør.

Vi tror på en vækstorienteret kultur – Growth Culture – hvor du som medarbejder får mulighed for at udvikle dig, komme med nye idéer og bidrage med nye idéer. Du bliver en del af et miljø med fleksible rammer, uformel tone og fokus på både faglig og personlig udvikling.

Med strategien” Brewing Tomorrow ”tager vi ansvar for bæredygtighed og fremtidens udfordringer. Vi tilbyder spændende karrieremuligheder – både i Danmark og internationalt.

Læs mere på http://www.carlsbergdanmark.dk

Interesseret?

Så send dit CV til os online. Du behøver ikke sende en ansøgning, men du bedes i dit CV inkludere et par sætninger om din motivation for at søge rollen.

I Carlsberg Danmark forpligter vi os til en inkluderende rekrutteringsproces og lige muligheder for alle. Vi ser mangfoldighed som en ressource, og opfordrer alle kandidater uanset alder, køn, baggrund og etnicitet til at søge.

For at sikre en så retfærdig rekrutteringsproces som muligt, bedes du undlade billede og navn i dit CV samt oplysninger omkring køn, uddannelsessted, alder og etnisk baggrund.

Ansøgningsfristen er den 11. oktober 2026.

Vil du høre mere om stillingen eller har du spørgsmål til stillingen, så er du velkommen til at kontakte BPM & Head of Admin & Process Development Andreas Utoft Jakobsen på tlf 28 96 61 42

Vi ser frem til at høre fra dig.

title: Become our new Quality Lead!
description:
Become our new Quality Lead!

Ready to help shape a culture of food safety, quality, and continuous improvement? Do you thrive in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where quality excellence is at the heart of everything we do? Then you might be our new Quality Lead at C&D Foods (Denmark) A/S!

About the position

As Quality Lead, you will become part of the Quality Department at C&D Foods Denmark and play a key role in supporting and maintaining the site's Food Safety and Quality Management Systems. You will work closely with teams such as Production, Engineering, R&D, Warehouse and Quality teams to ensure compliance with customer, legal and company standards while driving continuous improvement across the site.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced quality professional who enjoys leading quality initiatives, supporting audits, improving processes, and promoting a strong food safety culture.

Your key areas of responsibility:

  • Food Safety Culture & Training
  • Audits, Compliance & Continuous Improvement
  • Cleaning, Hygiene & Pest Control Management
  • Quality Assurance & Traceability

Examples of tasks could include:

  • Support and continuously improve the site’s Food Safety and Quality Management System (FSQMS), including HACCP and GMP
  • Participate in customer, regulatory and certification audits, as well as internal audit activities
  • Investigate non-conformances, customer complaints and quality issues, driving corrective actions
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to resolve food safety and quality challenges
  • Manage traceability systems, product testing programmes and external laboratory relationships
  • Lead site cleaning, hygiene and pest control programmes, ensuring compliance with relevant standards
  • Act as the key contact for cleaning chemical suppliers and support effective hygiene practices
  • Promote food safety culture, food defence initiatives and employee awareness programmes
  • Support Quality Supervisors and Quality Controllers while contributing to KPI performance and HACCP, traceability and audit teams

Candidate profile

  • Degree in Food Science, Food Technology, Biotechnology, Quality Management, or a related discipline
  • Experience in food quality, food safety or quality assurance within a manufacturing environment
  • Strong working knowledge of HACCP, food safety legislation and GFSI standards, including BRCGS
  • Experience with root cause analysis, risk assessments and continuous improvement tools
  • Internal Audit training
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office and quality management systems
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

We offer

You will become part of the C&D Foods family, an international company with a multicultural environment, across nationalities and cross-functional teams, where collaboration, diversity, and inclusion are part of everyday life. We prioritize employee well-being, work-life balance, and personal development.

We also offer health and dental insurance to all employees and value a workplace culture built on respect, openness, and genuine care, and just as importantly, we have a fun and informal atmosphere, with great energy and a good sense of humour across the entire site.

How to apply

Please send your CV along with a motivated application describing your interest in the position.

If you have any questions, you are welcome to contact:

Weronika Jasinski, HR Graduate

E-mail: Weronika.Jasinski@cdfoods.com

We kindly ask that all applications be submitted through our website only. Applications received by email will not be considered and will be permanently deleted upon receipt in accordance with GDPR requirements and our data protection procedures.

About C&D Foods

C&D Foods is one of Europe’s leading producers of private label pet food, manufacturing a wide range of both wet and dry food. The company’s headquarters are located in Mullingar, County Westmeath.

As part of ABP Food Group, C&D Foods has grown to become one of the industry’s leading pet food manufacturers.

C&D Foods currently operates 9 production facilities across 7 countries (Ireland, United Kingdom, France, Denmark, Austria, Spain, and the Netherlands) as well as 2 sales offices in Manchester and Italy.

title: Assistant Curator of Phycology
description:
Employment Type: Full-Time, Salary, Exempt
Deadline to Apply: This application will remain open until the position is filled.
Rate of Pay: $60,000.00 - $76,000.00 annually, commensurate with experience. The wage band is set and not subject to negotiation.

Job Purpose

The Assistant Curator in Natural Sciences initiates, develops, and directs original research projects related to biology and systematics; publishes original scholarly works; develops and enhances the Museum’s Natural Sciences collections within specialized and broad areas of the discipline; actively pursues funding support for research and Museum programs; and provides content and knowledge for, and actively engages with, Museum programs and activities.

Duties and Responsibilities

Research and Scholarship

  • Conducts original research related to Museum collections within specialized and broad scope of scientific discipline, including studies relevant to the Biodiversity of Hawai‘i (contributing to the Hawai‘i Biological Survey) and the broader Pacific region.

  • Maintains a moderate level of productivity in the publication of original scholarly works.

  • Maintains affiliations in scholarly and professional organizations through active service (i.e., committees, councils, editorial review boards, funding review panels), including presentations at regional, national, or international meetings, symposia, and workshops which enhance their development as a Museum scientific professional.

  • May serve in a junior editorial role for the Museum’s scholarly publications series.

Collections and Access

  • Assists in the development of Natural Sciences collections to improve and enhance the collections; works alongside the respective Collections Manager to assist in general oversight of collection management procedures (loan processing, accessions, cataloging, etc.); analyzes specimens and provides identifications within specialized scientific discipline.

  • Collaborates with Collections and Informatics staff to facilitate and enhance digital accessibility of collections, databases, and other resources in Natural Sciences.

  • Serves as a subject matter resource to inform and recommend updates to safety procedures and policies related to Natural Sciences collections, laboratories, field work, and associated research activities.

Funding and Project Oversight

  • Actively seeks and obtains financial support through grants, contracts, professional contracts and other resources to further research, bring improvements to Natural Sciences collections, and/or to support Museum programs.

  • Supervises grant-funded projects or laboratory staff and serves as affiliate faculty advisor to graduate level students as appropriate.

Public Programs and Education

  • Serves the Museum’s public programs and goals through contributions to educational program development, exhibit planning, and by providing lectures, workshops, field trips, staff and docent training and other activities; and through provision of technical information, content knowledge, and assistance to the Museum and its clients or partners.

Museum Engagement and Professional Practice

  • Contributes to operational planning, including planning and development of immediate and long-term project goals and objectives for the Department of Natural Sciences.

  • Interacts with staff and Museum clients with tact, courtesy, and professionalism. Demonstrates a collaborative approach; supports teamwork and maintains constructive working relationships with colleagues, clients, and partners.

  • Works in a safe manner and follows established safety practices to protect fellow staff members, volunteers, and visitors. Complies with applicable safety rules and regulations and establishes safe work practices. Promptly reports unsafe conditions, incidents, or accidents to appropriate individuals. Maintains assigned work areas and equipment in a manner that prioritizes safety and minimizes risk.

  • Performs other duties as requested to accomplish the goals of the Museum.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant biological discipline, with knowledge of collection-based and field-based studies of Biodiversity.

  • General knowledge of one or more groups of organisms occurring in Hawai‘i and/or the broader Pacific, and experience with comparative analytical methodologies relevant to the study of Biodiversity (e.g., comparative morphology, molecular systematics, biogeography, phylogenetic theory and practice, ecology, and/or conservation biology).

  • Understanding of the operations of a Natural Sciences collection, including preparation, preservation, storage, and management of preserved specimens, including aspects of collections conservation, acquisition, loans, exhibitions, and digitization.

  • Familiarity with appropriate field methods, techniques, and permissions for biotic surveys and other fieldwork.

  • Ability and interest in public engagement regarding the significance of their research program, Hawaiian and Pacific Biodiversity, and Museum priorities.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s Degree and/or PhD in a relevant biological discipline, with experience in collection-based and field-based studies of Biodiversity.

  • At least five years of experience in collection-based and field-based studies of Biodiversity.

  • Evidence of a developing research profile, demonstrated through publications, grant activity, or other professional recognition.

  • Experience in integrative systematic research involving genomic study of biodiversity and analysis of molecular data.

Other Requirements

  • The position is based on O‘ahu and requires regular, on-site presence for leadership and coordination of Museum operations.

  • Must maintain the ability to travel independently between Museum facilities, partner sites, and meetings; a valid driver’s license is required only if driving is necessary to perform job duties.

  • Must be willing to work a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends, to meet the needs of the organization and respond to operational priorities.

Direct Reports

Project-based, grant-funded staff

Working Conditions

Field work may involve exposure to high altitudes and wet conditions. Laboratory work environment may involve exposure to fumes, noxious odors, and gases from the mounting and preservation media, as well as dust and mold from the specimens themselves.

Physical Requirements

Primarily light work with periods of sitting, standing, walking, reaching, lifting, carrying, pushing, and pulling. Requires sustained hand eye coordination to use microscopes, hand tools, and light power tools to mount and prepare specimens ranging from small and delicate to large and heavy. Involves prolonged handling and manipulation of specimens and storage containers, extended periods of data entry and keyboard use, and visual acuity sufficient to perform detailed scientific work, including use of microscopes, depth perception, and the ability to distinguish colors, with or without reasonable accommodation. Requires the ability to communicate verbally and in writing with colleagues and others and the ability to lift and move up to 25 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation. May entail participation in field research activities in remote locations, including hiking, camping, climbing, SCUBA diving, working from boats or ships, transport via helicopter or small aircraft, and similar activities necessary to fulfill research objectives.

title: Business Developer - Category Contract Logistics, IKEA Supply Chain Operations
description:
Company description

At IKEA, we believe that we are better when we are physically together for collaboration, dialogues, and conversations. We believe in the power of human interactions, the informal chats, the energy, belonging, and creativity generated by people being in the same place. Our approach is that we spend most of our time in the IKEA workplace, with the flexibility to work from home.

Our vision is to create a better everyday life for the many people. We do this by offering a wide range of well-designed, functional home furnishing and food products at prices so low that as many people as possible will be able to afford them.


Supply Chain Operations is a global business unit within IKEA Supply, connecting customers with IKEA products in a simple, affordable, and sustainable way. With over 700 co-workers, we lead, plan, and execute the supply of products between suppliers and retailers. We deliver excellent transport and logistics solutions by optimizing replenishment, managing goods flow, sourcing and developing transport and logistics capacities, and securing supply quality.


Category Contract Logistics is responsible for sourcing and operating outsourced warehouses and logistics services at optimal cost, while meeting high service and quality standards. We ensure safety, security, and sustainability, continuously contributing to the IKEA vision. Operating in one of the most dynamic areas of logistics, we embrace innovation and technology to keep improving.
To support our growth in South and Southeast Asia, we are now looking for a Business Developer to join our team in Port Klang, Malaysia.


Job description

We are looking for a skilled and motivated person to source, negotiate and develop our warehousing and logistics partnerships, and to make sure they deliver strong performance for IKEA customers. Our team sources, implements and develops solutions that balance total supply chain cost with service level, capacity and sustainability.


As a Business Developer, you will play a key role in shaping the future of IKEA’s logistics network.
You will own a portfolio of external logistics service providers end to end: sourcing new solutions, implementing them together with the team, and driving your service provider’s day-to-day performance against clear targets for cost, quality, lead time and capacity utilisation. You will secure the business objectives set out in the Category Contract Logistics business plan and build service providers that perform today and are ready for tomorrow. Your work connects directly to three of our business priorities:
• Low cost: you deliver year-on-year cost development across your portfolio and take waste out of the value chain, so we offer better service at a lower total cost.
• Growth: you secure reliable, flexible warehouse capacity that scales as our volumes grow and our network changes.
• Accessibility for the many people: by making the supply chain more affordable and more available, you help bring IKEA within reach of even more people.
This is a full-time role based in our office in Port Klang, Malaysia, reporting to the Business Development Manager, Contract Logistics.


Qualification
  • Lead commercial activities and negotiations, securing competitive agreements aligned with our business plans.
  • Build and maintain a strong portfolio of logistics service providers, ensuring alignment with long-term business needs.
  • Take overall responsibility for implementing new solutions together with the team, ensuring a smooth start-up, and steer day-to-day performance so that service providers consistently deliver against KPIs on cost, quality, lead time and utilisation.
  • Drive continuous development of both the business and service providers, embracing innovation and future-focused solutions.
  • Identify and act on new business opportunities, participate in tenders, and create conditions for cost optimisation and sustainable growth.
  • Stay ahead of the market: monitor industry trends, cost drivers, and legal frameworks; share insights and turn them into action.
  • Develop and implement annual action plans with service providers to achieve strategic objectives and measurable results.
  • Ensure compliance with agreements, IWAY standards and Supply Chain Security requirements, and internal processes and ways of working.
  • Represent IKEA as a trusted business partner, always acting with a value- and fact-based approach.

We are looking for someone who combines expertise, curiosity and a strong business mindset:

  • Solid knowledge of logistics, including contract logistics, warehousing, and distribution with a clear understanding of warehousing’s role, cost structure and key drivers in the supply chain.
  • Strong awareness of market conditions and cost drivers in South and Southeast Asia.
  • Proven ability to optimise supply chain costs and deliver value, supported by excellent negotiation skills.
  • Comfortable using data analytics and finance to drive business decisions and improvements through facts and insights.
  • Legal knowledge related to logistics and warehousing agreements.
  • Exceptional presentation and communication skills and ability to influence and engage diverse stakeholders.
  • Collaborative team player who thrives in cross-functional, international environments.
  • Self-driven and highly organised, able to manage multiple priorities and act as a change driver.
  • University degree in logistics, economics, or business administration, with at least 5 years of relevant experience.
  • Fluent in English, both spoken and written.
  • Proficiency in tools such as Excel, Power BI and PowerPoint.
  • Experience with IKEA Supply Chain and leading cross-functional, cross-cultural initiatives is a plus.

More Information

Why Join Us


We believe in you. You will lead your assignment in a diverse team, partnering with world-class service providers and driving continuous improvement in logistics.
We grow with you. In regular conversations with your manager, you can explore your development and career opportunities, and we will support you on the way. We embrace making mistakes and learning from them. For us at IKEA, this is the best way forward.
We develop together. We listen, build strong relationships, and help our partners grow to their full potential.

Recruitment Process

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, we would love to hear from you! The selection process is ongoing, so please submit your application in English as soon as possible, no later than 7 October 2026.

title: Journeyman Powerline Technician
description:
Forbes Bros. Group of Companies delivers transmission, distribution, substation, and related power infrastructure projects across Canada and the United States.

Our work spans field construction, project delivery, operations, and corporate support in an environment where safety, execution, and reliability matter.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Journeyman Powerline Technician (PLT) will assist in the construction and maintenance of distribution powerlines. The Journeyman Lineman will have a valid Journeyperson certificate and previous experience in the distribution or transmission industry as a Journeyman Lineman. The candidate will demonstrate strong knowledge of distribution powerline construction, problem-solving skills, organizational skills, and share our core value of “we work safe.”

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Field Duties & Compliance

  • Install, inspect, maintain, and repair high- and low-voltage distribution systems.
  • Troubleshoot and repair overhead and underground distribution lines.
  • Construct new distribution powerlines across all phases, including framing of wood and steel structures.
  • Perform conductor stringing and cable pulling in overhead and civil environments.
  • Support setup and operation of pulling and tensioning equipment.
  • Operate various equipment used in the construction and maintenance of distribution powerlines.
  • Maintain interior, exterior, overhead, and underground electrical distribution systems.

Safety Leadership & Compliance

  • Ensure all safety protocols are followed, including PPE usage, permitting, and safe work practices.
  • Participate in incident reporting, safety observations, and corrective action implementation.
  • Lead by example in promoting a positive safety culture within the crew.

Quality Assurance & Task Readiness

  • Complete work in accordance with specifications, drawings, and client requirements.
  • Identify non-conforming work and communicate issues to supervision for timely resolution.
  • Assist in preparing work areas for inspections and client walkdowns.

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement

  • Contribute to safety improvement initiatives and maintain a strong safety-first mindset.
  • Participate in Safety, Quality, and Production meetings.
  • Participate in tailboard meetings.
  • Support the training and development of apprentices and new team members.

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

  • Red Seal certification in the powerline industry from an accredited trade school, or equivalent combination of education and experience in the powerline industry
  • Valid Class 5 driver’s licence required; Class 1A driver’s licence is preferred
  • Strong understanding of construction and maintenance principles, methods, and procedures
  • Commitment to working safely, with the ability to recognize hazards and apply the hierarchy of controls to eliminate risks in both field and office environments
  • Strong listening, problem-solving, and time management skills with the ability to meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to interact professionally with team members, supervision, and stakeholders
  • Ability to work independently or as part of a team with minimal supervision
  • Willingness and ability to travel and work frequent overtime and weekend hours to meet project schedules and operational requirements
  • Physically fit and able to perform manual labour in varying weather conditions and environments, including heavy lifting

Forbes Bros. Group of Companies and its affiliated entities are committed to providing a respectful and accessible recruitment process.

Employment is subject to the requirements of the applicable role, location, project, and employing entity. Depending on the position, this may include verification of work authorization, background screening, driver abstract, drug and alcohol screening, credential verification, client/site access requirements, and other pre-employment conditions permitted by applicable law.

Applicants who require accommodation during the recruitment process are encouraged to contact the recruitment team.

title: Financial Crime Prevention Specialist & proceskonsulent til EIFO
description:
Har du erfaring i krydsfeltet mellem Financial Crime Prevention og IT? Og ønsker du at bruge dine kompetencer i en rolle, hvor du gør en forskel både i rollen og gennem de aktiviteter, som kendetegner os? Så er du måske vores nye Financial Crime Prevention Specialist og proceskonsulent i Danmarks Eksport- og Investeringsfond (EIFO).

Som led i styrkelsen af EIFOs Financial Crime Prevention-område søger vi en ny specialist, der kan skabe sammenhæng mellem forretning, processer, data og systemer. Rollen er nyoprettet og indgår i et tværfagligt team med ansvar for at udvikle og modne FCP-området på tværs af organisationen.

Din rolle

Som vores nye Financial Crime Prevention (FCP) Specialist er du bindeleddet mellem FCP og IT. Du tager bredt ejerskab for FCP-processerne og formidler effektivt de behov, FCP-området har, til de kolleger du samarbejder med i IT og forretningsudvikling.

I rollen arbejder du med at omsætte regulatoriske krav og forretningsbehov til konkrete løsninger, der understøtter en effektiv og sammenhængende FCP-værdikæde. Sammen med kolleger på tværs af organisationen bidrager du til at identificere forbedringsmuligheder og sikre, at udviklingen sker med et end-to-end perspektiv på tværs af hele området.

Du refererer til Head of FCP.

Dine kompetencer

  • Bred og dyb faglighed – du har dyb indsigt i sædvanlige FCP-processer, herunder KYC, ODD og EDR. Derudover har du et godt kendskab til sanktionsscreening og ABC.
  • Erfaring med samarbejde med IT – du er vant til at samarbejde med IT-folk og ”taler deres sprog”. På den måde kan du bidrage til effektive og værdiskabende forandringer.
  • Du trives med kompleksitet – du anerkender, at kompleksitet og udfordringer i systemlandskab, datagrundlag og processer er et vilkår, og fokuserer på løsninger fremfor problemer.
  • Proces- og udviklingsorienteret – du kan kortlægge eksisterende arbejdsgange, identificere forbedringsmuligheder og omsætte regulatoriske og forretningsmæssige behov til konkrete løsninger.
  • Forretningsorienteret – du evner at se sammenhængen mellem regulatoriske krav, operationelle processer og tekniske løsninger og omsætter dette til konkrete forbedringer.
  • Kollegial - du skal arbejde sammen med kolleger på tværs af afdelinger, så det er vigtigt, at du er god til relationer og bidrager til motivation og godt humør i dine samarbejdsrelationer.
  • Kundefokus – du er fuldt bevidst om, at compliance med FCP-krav skal kombineres med de bedst mulige kundeprocesser.

I EIFO er FCP en del af kreditområdet, som ud over kredit også omfatter økonomiske analyser og ESG.

Hvem er du?

Vi forestiller os, at du har:

  • En baggrund som bankuddannet, jurist eller økonom kombineret med praktisk erfaring inden for AML/CTF, sanktioner og ABC i et pengeinstitut
  • Solid erfaring med samarbejde med IT på FCP-området
  • God erfaring med procesudvikling, implementering af nye løsninger eller større forandringsinitiativer
  • Gode kommunikationsevner
  • Lyst til at skabe resultater og gøre en forskel
  • Motivation til at arbejde i krydsfeltet mellem faglig specialisering, forretning og teknologi

Vores værdier

Du bliver kulturbærer for EIFOs tre værdier:

  • Enkelhed – du bidrager til overblik og tydelige prioriteringer
  • Forretningsfokus – du sikrer, at vi udvikler det rigtige, ikke bare det mulige
  • Tillid – du fremmer åbenhed, faglighed og samarbejde

Det tilbyder vi – klart formål og attraktive vilkår

I EIFO arbejder du for dansk erhvervslivs fremtid – og du får mulighed for at skabe reel værdi for virksomheder, der driver vækst, grøn omstilling og innovation.

Du får:

  • Et spændende og udfordrende job med et klart formål og stor samfundsmæssig betydning
  • En arbejdsplads præget af forretningsfokus, enkelhed og tillid i en uhøjtidelig kontekst
  • Attraktive vilkår, fleksibilitet og plads til både ambition og balance i arbejdslivet
  • Engagerede og fagligt dygtige kolleger i en mangfoldig og inkluderende kultur, hvor forskellighed ses som en styrke.

Er det dig, vi leder efter?

Send din ansøgning og CV snarest muligt og senest den 17. oktober 2026. Samtaler forventes at blive afholdt løbende.

Som led i vores arbejde med inkluderende rekruttering beder vi dig venligst om ikke at inkludere billede, alder og civilstand i dit ansøgningsmateriale.

Forløbet omfatter to samtalerunder, hvor anden runde indeholder assessments (logik- og personlighedsanalyse). Referencer indhentes efter aftale, og straffeattest skal fremvises ved ansættelse. Tiltrædelse tilstræbes hurtigst muligt.

Vil du vide mere? Kontakt Anna Lynge Nielsen, Senior Talent Acquisition Partner, på alni@eifo.dk eller +45 20 68 03 92.

Hos EIFO tror vi på, at diversitet skaber bedre løsninger – derfor opfordrer vi alle kvalificerede kandidater til at søge.

Vi ser frem til at høre fra dig!

Om Danmarks Eksport- og Investeringsfond

Danmarks Eksport- og Investeringsfond (EIFO) er danske virksomheders fælles indgang til risikovillig statslig finansiering. Vi har et samlet forretningsomfang på omkring 180 mia. kr. og har knap 500 medarbejdere. Med professionalisme og internationalt udsyn arbejder vi hver dag for at understøtte de erhvervssucceser, der kan gøre Danmark rigere på det, der gør en forskel. EIFO er Danmarks nationale erhvervsfremmende bank, investeringsfond og Danmarks officielle eksportkreditinstitut i én og samme finansielle institution.

title: Binance Accelerator Programm - Software Engineer (KYB)

title: Head of Discipline - Power Supply
description:
**Do you want to turn strategy into action, inspire people, and lead with purpose? Can you translate goals into clear direction and build an engaged, collaborative team? And do you want to play a key role in advancing rail electrification in Denmark? Then you might be our new Head of Discipline for Power Supply.

**Create the solutions that enable a better tomorrow
We are seeking a Head of Discipline for Power Supply to lead our skilled team of 20 colleagues. As part of the Rail leadership team within Transportation, you will work closely with other Heads of Discipline to develop our people, strengthen our capabilities, and deliver complex projects.
Together with our clients, we deliver some of the most impactful rail infrastructure projects in Denmark, including the Danish electrification programme, future S-trains in Copenhagen, and a diverse portfolio of both major and local rail projects. Our work supports railway electrification, traction power systems, catenary systems, and power supply solutions that contribute to the modernisation and green transition of the Danish railway sector.
In this role, you will support both people development and project success while ensuring that engagement, well-being, and inclusion remain at the heart of your leadership.

Your key responsibilities will be:

  • Manage the discipline on a day-to-day basis, including 1:1s, recruitment, and onboarding activities
  • Support the Resource Manager in workforce planning
  • Work closely with the Head of Engineering to set the direction for the discipline, including clear targets for performance and employee development
  • Be responsible for promoting employee engagement and encouraging a productive, diverse, and inclusive culture
  • Be involved in projects as a technical lead within your area of expertise
  • Oversee the Power Supply agenda within Rail and collaborate with the business development team to build and grow the discipline

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future
Like us, you believe that leadership success comes from setting a clear and meaningful direction for your team and supporting them in being responsible for their work. You always delegate responsibility and ensure an open and safe dialogue, and you coach your people to achieve their aspirations through constructive, fact-based feedback. Attracting and developing a diverse group of high-potential team members is at the top of your agenda, as is creating an inclusive, supportive and trusting culture in your team.

On top of that, you will have:

  • People management experience as either project manager or line manager
  • Solid experience with railway projects, either as infrastructure owner, supplier, contractor or consultant.
  • Experience within rail electrification, traction power, power supply systems or related electrical infrastructure.
  • Professional proficiency in English and Danish.

A place to work and so much more
At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers. We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Got more questions?
If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Jens Meyer, Head of Engineering, at JSMR@cowi.com
Get to know us even better at our website, , where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

Before you apply
All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key.
We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

title: Auto Painter - Haines City, FL
description:
We’re looking for Auto Painters with a minimum of 1 year of professional automotive painting experience to join us at Carvana - the fastest-growing used automotive retailer in U.S. history and one of the four fastest companies to make the Fortune 500.

As a Painter, you’ll be expected to prime vehicles and perform final sanding before the vehicle is painted, along with buffing, touch-up, paint mixing, and airbrush.

At Carvana, you’ll receive a competitive wage and amazing perks – including a 401(k) with Carvana match and even a vehicle purchase discount – all while using state of the art tools in one of our high-tech Inspection Centers (click here to learn more). If you’re joining us in an entry-level position, we offer training programs to make sure your skills and pay progress along with the company.

Other perks of the Job

  • 100% company-paid healthcare premiums
  • Generous paid-time off and your birthday is a holiday!
  • ASE and tool reimbursement programs
  • Tuition reimbursement and student loan repayment

Schedule:

We do everything we can to deliver an exceptional customer experience, and that includes delivering great vehicles when expected. If we're in a pinch, mandatory overtime is one way in which we can follow-through on this commitment to our customers. We're looking for team players who are all in on our mission and are able to work mandatory overtime based on our business needs.

How To Get Started
Join the Carvana team by applying on this page, or call one of our recruiters by phone at (888) 690-7853, Monday through Friday, between 6 AM and 4 PM PT (9AM to 7PM ET).

Not a match for this role?
We have a variety of paint roles available, depending on your experience - look below to see other roles available to help us get our low-mileage, late-model cars ready for our customers:

  • Paint Prepper (min 6 months professional experience): prepare vehicles for cosmetic paintwork, including sanding, masking, taping, bagging, unbagging/tear down, and buffing
  • Entry-Level Painter (min 1 year professional experience): prime vehicles and perform final sanding before the vehicle is painted, along with buffing, touch-up, paint mixing, and airbrush.
  • Mid-Level Painter (min 3 years professional experience): match/mix paint color and use water-based paint to paint the vehicle inside our paint booths
  • Experienced Painter (min 5 years professional experience): painting (base coats, tri-coats, solid, metallic, and clear coats), blending adjacent panels, and paint correcting vehicles.

We also have a variety of other automotive roles available in one of our 18 locations across the country – take a look at our Careers site to apply for one of the following roles:

  • Auto Body roles: Paint, Prep/Body work, Wheel Repair, Airbrush, Interior Repair, Glass Repair, and PDR (Paintless Dent Repair) roles
  • Auto Technician/Mechanic roles: Lube and Oil, Inspection, Brake and Tire, Mechanical Repair / Build, and Master Technician roles
  • Entry-Level roles: Detailing, Inventory Associate (Car Porters), Photo, Parts Associate, Inspection, and Coordinator/Administrator roles

General qualifications and requirements

  • Ability to physically operate vehicle equipment and tools - must be able to lift up to 60 pounds independently
  • Must be at least 18 years of age and possess a valid driver’s license. Some positions may be subject to an Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check
  • An ability to work in a fast-paced, ever-changing production environment while sometimes being exposed to excessive weather conditions (heat/cold)
  • Use of safety equipment that may include but not limited to face shield or goggles, non-slip shoes, gloves, mask, and other protective garments and equipment

About Carvana
At Carvana, we sell cars but we aren’t car salesmen. Our promise is simple: we won’t sell a car to a customer that we wouldn’t sell to our own Mom. Period.

To make sure our cars are in first-rate condition, we’ve built multiple vehicle Reconditioning Centers around the country, where our cars are inspected, perfected, and photographed before reaching the Carvana website.

Think you’ve got what it takes to join our team? Apply today!

Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer. All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law. Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Must be at least 18 years of age and possess a valid driver’s license. Must be able to read, write, speak and understand English.

title: Program Manager, Carrier Management, AGL, Exports Supply Chain

Amazon.com is seeking qualified candidates to join our Cross Border Exports Logistics team. Amazon.com reaches customers around the globe on all seven continents, and are in need of individuals who want to help ensure a fast cost effective solution to delivering packages to every far reach of the world. Do you obsess over how to improve processes to deliver a superior customer experience? Do the words “that can’t be done”, drive you to find a solution for how “that can be done”? A successful candidate will be able to show proven results in developing action plans as well as improvements implemented as a result of those plans. Additionally a successful candidate will be able to display strength influencing cross functional teams to take action on the data, as well as developing action items to improve results over the short and long term.

title: Senior Research Associate, Histology (Contract)
description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION

Mirai Bio is a privately-held, Flagship-founded biotechnology company that is delivering genetic medicines from promise to performance. Mirai was built to solve one of the field’s central challenges: achieving precise, scalable delivery of diverse nucleic acid payloads to specific cells and tissues, particularly beyond the liver. By combining a large and growing proprietary in vivo biodistribution dataset, machine learning-guided lipid nanoparticle optimization, modular targeted particle design, and integrated translation and manufacturing capabilities, Mirai helps partners accelerate development, reduce technical risk, and pursue high-value programs making delivery a strategic advantage. We are seeking collaborative, relentless problem solvers that share our passion for defining the future of genetic medicines together.

THE ROLE

We are seeking a Senior Research Associate, Histology contractor to join the Platform Group at Mirai Bio to support laboratory research activities towards development of novel technologies enabling next generation genomic medicines. The successful candidate will have a strong understanding of the technical and equipment needs in a lab as well as significant hands-on experience with standard histology, cell culturing and in vitro cell biology techniques. They will work independently and as part of a collaborative team.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Performing laboratory assays and tasks including processing tissues for histology, plate-based reporter assays and additional in vitro assays
  • Review data slides to streamline optimization and data analysis of immune histochemistry and immuno florescence readouts
  • Help manage external vendors and CRO in support of histology assays
  • Developing new assays or optimizing existing ones based on in-depth knowledge of laboratory techniques.
  • Analyzing and accurately documenting assay results in an electronic lab notebook or other technical reporting formats

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS

  • BS or MS in Biology, Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, or related scientific discipline
    • BS + 5 years of relevant industry or research experience
    • MS + 3 years of relevant industry or research experience
  • Previous experience with histology evaluation and in vitro cell based assays is required
  • Strong cell culture experience, including experience executing protocols, troubleshooting assays is preferred
  • Prior experience working with lipid nanoparticles is a plus

Knowledge and Experience

Preferred Skills

  • Technology and/or application support.

Funko is a purveyor of pop culture and licensed-focused collectibles company. Vinyl is the number one stylized vinyl collectible on the market, selling millions of figures to fans around the world.

What You’ll Do

  • Bring the vision to life through consistent, clear, and proactive daily communication with Design, Licensing, factories, and cross functional partners aligning expectations, resolving issues early, and ensuring every product moves smoothly and efficiently from concept to creation
  • Own and strategically drive the Loungefly development calendar, ensuring alignment across design, licensing, approvals, sourcing, and production to deliver on-time, on-brand product launches.

  • Champion the licensor approval journey by managing the full licensor approval workflow, including concept submissions in proprietary portals, sample approvals, packaging, and final production signoffs.
  • Strengthen and build licensor relationships by serving as the primary point of contact for assigned licensors fostering trusted and collaborative partnerships through clear communication, responsiveness, and a deep understanding of licensor goals, brand standards, and long term business objectives.
  • Partner with our art team to guarantee assets are delivered on time, meet licensor expectations, and align with initial design submissions, all while ensuring costs hit the mark.
  • Create detailed, factory ready tech packs that include materials, BOMs, EOQs, product instructions, and timelines. Will update and refine technical documents as products evolve.
  • Serve as the go to technical expert for factory partners, answering questions and clarifying specs and patternmaking, knowing what’s feasible and how to adjust to stay within manufacturing limits.
  • Review and approve all samples and packaging from silhouettes to stickers, providing clear feedback to ensure every detail is accurate, on-brand, high quality, and licensor approved before production.
  • Collaborate closely with the Quality and Compliance teams to identify risks early, resolve issues, coordinate product testing, and ensure documentation is complete across licensor platforms and internal systems.

What You’ll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Product Development, Technical Design, Industrial/Fashion Design, or related field, or 5+ years of relevant experience in accessories, apparel or footwear.
  • Proven ability to manage the full product development lifecycle, from design handoff and technical development through sampling, costing, testing, and production approval.
  • Strong ability to translate design intent into technically executable products, with expertise in accessories construction, measurements, materials, hardware, finishes, and functionality.
  • Strong knowledge of accessories materials and manufacturing, including leather, PU/synthetics, textiles, trims, hardware, embossing, printing, and related construction techniques.
  • Experienced in sample review and technical evaluation, identifying construction, measurement, workmanship, quality, and functional issues and providing clear, actionable factory comments.
  • Experience working directly with domestic and international factories and vendors, including tanneries, mills, and hardware/trim suppliers; skilled in troubleshooting, cost/value engineering, and manufacturability.
  • Working knowledge of product testing, quality standards, and performance requirements, with the ability to proactively identify and resolve material, construction, hardware, and production risks.
  • Highly organized and able to manage multiple styles and seasonal developments, partnering with Design, Merchandising, Sourcing, and QA to meet key development milestones.
  • Proficient in Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, Excel, and PLM systems; experience with 3D development/CAD (CLO, Rhino, or similar) and licensed product development is a plus.

Salary Information

The base salary range for this position in the selected city is $73,000-$92,000 annually. Compensation may vary outside of this range depending on several factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies and experience, and location. Base pay is one part of the Total Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work, and this role may be eligible for additional discretionary bonuses/incentives, and restricted stock units.

Funko offers a competitive compensation package with full benefits and a 401(K) plan with matching contributions from the company. Most importantly, we offer a creative work environment with people who love pop culture just as much as you do. Can’t wait to gush about your latest binge? Neither can we! Looking for a place where your favorite pop culture t-shirt will receive the compliments it deserves? We know how you feel!

title: Jr./Mid-Level RF Compatibility Test Engineer - Space Programs
description:
Responsibilities

We are seeking an RF Compatibility Test Engineer to support our NASA customer in Greenbelt, MD. Peraton is the Prime Contractor on the SENSE Contract; responsible for the Operations, Maintenance, Sustainment and Systems Engineering of satellite communication systems for NASA.

In this position your work will involve providing spacecraft to ground station compatibility testing, engineering testing, and integration support for missions, projects, systems, and ground network transitions and initiatives. Maintain and operate test and networking systems within a Compatibility Test Lab (CTL), a testing facility located at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC). The CTL is used for prelaunch testing, engineering and proof of concept testing for the NASA Space Relay (SR) and Direct-To-Earth (DTE) network.

The work will include engineering troubleshooting, fault detection, and isolation. This position will also be responsible for the following:

  • Perform testing (in accordance with test plans) with the SR and DTE to confirm RF compatibility of user spacecraft and the supporting ground network interfaces in accordance with test requirements and procedures.
    • Review requirements, test plans and procedures.
    • Setup and checkout equipment in test configurations.
    • Setup and checkout various equipment interfaces such as local network interfaces, data and clock inputs and outputs, frequency standard references, RF signal levels and fiber optics.
    • Support test team with knowledge of test procedures.
    • Gather and summarize test results.
  • Perform testing as described in Compatibility Test Plans. These tests may include travel to off-site locations such as spacecraft manufacturing sites, ground tracking stations, and/or Mission Operations Control Centers to emulate communication links between user spacecraft and the DTE and/or the SR.
  • Perform radio frequency (RF) testing so that the measurement points are accessible through either RF or baseband interfaces and validate real-time authentication of telemetry, command and ranging systems.
  • Perform signal investigation such as unique engineering tests for new modulation/demodulation techniques, new hardware, configurations; proof of concept testing for new antenna systems.
  • Provide support in the acquisition, maintenance, and protection of resources in order to ensure that space communications systems can operate to their fullest capacity.
  • Contribute to the ongoing modernization of the test environment by assisting with development or integration of networking and of increasingly automated procedures.
  • Develop code to integrate COTS software into test automation suite
    • Data collection
    • Reporting
  • Develop test procedures in accordance with test automation efforts
  • Refine reporting templates to align with data collection

#HIRE4SENSE

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Associate’s Degree in Engineering/Science/Math or related technical discipline and 2 years of related technical experience; without a degree, 6+ years of related experience is required
  • Knowledge of RF systems: frequency bands, purpose of RF devices, measures, signal distortion
  • RF engineering skills which include the ability to independently configure and operate RF test equipment: Spec An, Sig Gen, Oscilloscope
  • Experience with configuring and operating baseband devices: modems, routers, switches
  • Experience writing test plans, test set-up, interpreting results and explaining to others
  • Knowledge of coding and modulation techniques
  • Experience with MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, Visio and MS Word
  • Ability to obtain a DOD secret clearance.
  • Must be a US citizen.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience and knowledge of NASA’s SN and NEN Networks and associated communication systems.
  • Experienced with Ethernet communications
  • Knowledge of scripting (Python or similar)
  • Experience with COSMOS software
  • Able to work both independently and collaboratively in groups
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, including presentation skills

Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

$51,000 - $82,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. title: Resident Entertainment Director
description:
The Entertainment Director will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and hosting weekly resident events and quarterly large events while obtaining sponsorships. They will also be responsible for marketing the properties and attending marketing events in the area to promote our luxury apartment communities. This role requires experience in coordinating logistics and handling multiple vendors to create large events.


The Entertainment Director will report to ownership weekly on future events, successes of previous events and suggest new, out of the box ideas to engage residents in the community social entertainment. On matters of budget and community-specific needs, the Entertainment Director reports to the Community Manager at each community. All work will be done under personal responsibility, with no local direct manager managing time or projects. The Entertainment Director is responsible for getting all reports and events executed on time and as planned. Assistance will be provided by office and maintenance staff as requested and will be managed by the Entertainment Director. The purpose of this role is to create a community environment, a sense of home and lifestyle that makes residents want to renew, and invite their friends to move in as well. Below is a more detailed look at specific responsibilities and tasks of this position.


Event Planning and Execution

  • Create visually appealing event calendars for print and digital distribution.
  • Purchase supplies, manage event setup and breakdown, and host events with a focus on creating a welcoming and engaging atmosphere for residents.

Communication and Coordination

  • Maintain communication with leasing staff to ensure they are informed of upcoming events and have materials ready for residents.

Marketing and Partner Collaboration

  • Foster relationships with local businesses to secure event sponsorships and contributions.
  • Assist leasing teams in developing and promoting open houses and creative marketing initiatives.
  • Attend Chamber of Commerce events to network and organize hosted events.
  • Manage social media postings to promote events and highlight community engagement.

Community and Staff Engagement

  • Engage with residents during events, fostering connections and encouraging participation.
  • Organize pre-event meetings to assign responsibilities and ensure all staff, including maintenance, are prepared for larger events.
  • Support fitness programs by coordinating with instructors and promoting events within the community.

Administrative Tasks

  • Manage event supplies using a petty cash card and ensure all expenses are accurately recorded in the system.
  • Oversee community garden programs (where available), managing sign-ups, assignments, and resident communication.
  • Provide weekly recaps of event attendance, images, and feedback to stakeholders.
