title: Investment Director - Growth
description:
The Export and Investment Fund of Denmark (EIFO) is looking for an experienced Investment Director – Growth to join our growth investment team and help scale the next generation of Danish & European technology leaders.

Our purpose – scaling the companies that shape tomorrow

EIFO is Denmark’s sovereign investment fund, providing long-term capital to startups, scaleups, and growth stage companies. This role sits in Direct Venture & Growth, which deploys significant capital into high potential scaleups with proven traction and global ambitions. We invest across sectors, while life science remains the primary vertical on the venture side.

We work closely with founders, leadership teams, and co-investors to support governance, international expansion, and strategic decision making. To bolster our senior capacity, we are now seeking an Investment Director who can manage major transactions and represent EIFO in high stakes boardrooms.

Your new role

As Investment Director – Growth, you will identify, evaluate, structure, and execute EIFO’s larger growth investments — typically Series B+ and beyond. You will play a central role in shaping EIFO’s growth strategy, supporting portfolio companies at board level, and ensuring disciplined capital allocation.

You will collaborate across EIFO’s investment tracks and engage with Danish and international founders, executives, and investors.

Your key responsibilities in this role can be grouped into four sections:

1) Investment & capital allocation

  • Lead and own major growth investments from sourcing to closing.
  • Structure minority positions with robust governance and downside protection.
  • Underwrite scale risks across execution, organisation, markets, and capital structure.
  • Develop and maintain advanced financial models (Excel proficiency required).

2) Board work & value creation

  • Represent EIFO as a board member or active observer.
  • Support CEOs and leadership teams with:
    • Internationalisation strategies
    • Governance and reporting
    • Capital planning and longterm financing
  • Facilitate clear, constructive discussions on performance, strategy, and leadership.

3) Portfolio & exit

  • Monitor growth stage portfolio companies and key value drivers.
  • Assess exit scenarios (M&A, IPOs, secondaries).
  • Contribute to disciplined capital recycling.

4) Strategic development

  • Co-develop EIFO’s growth investment model.
  • Ensure smooth transitions from early stage to growth stage investment tracks.
  • Enhance EIFO’s role as a long-term institutional growth partner.

Who you are

You have deep experience in growth investing and thrive in complex ownership and board environments. You combine methodical analytical discipline with commercial judgement and bring a measured, conviction-driven approach.

The ideal candidate has:

  • 10–15+ years from:
    • Growth equity / late-stage VC / PE light, or
    • Corporate venture with real ownership responsibility
  • Demonstrated ability to:
    • Lead large investment checks and complex minority deals
    • Navigate advanced capital structures and investor rights
    • Operate in high-pressure board environments
    • Scale companies internationally (EU/US)
  • Advanced analytical skills, including advanced Excel modelling
  • Low ego, high conviction mindset and ability to say no when needed
  • Understanding of institutional mandates and long-term capital responsibility
  • Advantage: Experience in defence, dual-use tech, or complex industrial technologies.

Why join EIFO?

  • Be part of a mission-driven organization at the heart of Denmark’s investment ecosystem, helping shape the future of innovation.
  • Lead impactful investment projects and collaborate with a skilled, diverse team.
  • Have the opportunity to influence strategic investment decisions while working in a dynamic and evolving environment.
  • Access substantial capital and resources to execute your ideas and initiatives.
  • Work in a collaborative and supportive environment where both your leadership and administrative contributions will be valued.

Are you our next colleague?

The recruitment process is managed by Heidrick & Struggles. Please submit your application and CV to ansogning@heidrick.com no later than October 8, 2026.

EIFO encourages candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Let’s build the future together.

About Denmark’s Export and Investment Fund

Export and Investment Fund of Denmark (EIFO) is the single entry point for companies seeking Danish state-backed financing. We manage a portfolio worth approximately USD 30 billion and employ close to 500 staff. EIFO serves as Denmark’s official export credit agency, national promotional bank, and investment fund, all in one financial institution.

title: Senior Sourcing Associate
description:
About Ruggable:

Ruggable is a leading direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand based in Los Angeles, California with an extraordinary track record of high, profitable growth. We pride ourselves on having an extremely loyal customer base and a talented team made up of genuinely caring people who take action and deliver results. We are venture-backed and own a patented washable rug design that's disrupting the home décor industry. Our mission is to empower our customers to live vibrantly with beautiful products that don't compromise on function. If you're passionate about consumer products, e-commerce, and high-growth start-ups, keep reading!

Job Summary: The Senior Sourcing Associate will lead the development, and commercialization of white label products that expand and strengthen the Ruggable assortment. This role will partner closely with Creative, Design, Merchandising, and Operations to identify assortment opportunities and translate them into compelling, brand-right product offerings. This role will leverage the capabilities, constructions, and product offerings of global suppliers, identifying products that can be customized, and adapted through a Ruggable lens. The Senior Sourcing Associate will be responsible for finding the right suppliers and product solutions, applying Ruggable standards, and managing the development process from initial product identification through production.

The ideal candidate combines a strong product eye with deep sourcing and product development experience, understands how to evaluate supplier capabilities and commercially viable products, and can move quickly from assortment opportunity to market-ready product.

What You’ll Do:
• Lead white label sourcing, product development and commercialization from initial assortment opportunity through production and launch.
• Partner closely with Merchandising and Creative teams to identify gaps and opportunities within the existing assortment and translate those needs into actionable product and sourcing strategies.
• Research global markets, suppliers, manufacturing regions, trade shows, and emerging product categories to identify new products, materials, constructions, and vendor capabilities.
• Identify and onboard new suppliers capable of filling specific assortment needs while meeting Ruggable standards.
• Evaluate existing supplier product lines and capabilities to identify products that can be customized, or adapted to align with Ruggable’s design sensibility and customer expectations.
• Develop clear product briefs for suppliers that communicate aesthetic direction, target costs, quality expectations, performance requirements, and key commercial objectives.
• Own the development process with global suppliers, including sampling, revisions, costing, testing, approvals, pre-production requirements, and final production specifications.
• Ensure product is fully commercialized and all critical product information is finalized prior to bulk PO issuance.
• Build detailed development calendars and critical paths, ensuring suppliers and internal stakeholders remain aligned to key milestones and launch dates.
• Negotiate product costs, MOQs, lead times, payment terms, and other commercial requirements while protecting the intended product value and quality..
• Evaluate samples for aesthetic execution, construction, quality, functionality, performance, and overall alignment with the intended product brief.
• Partner with Quality, Testing, and Compliance teams to ensure white label products meet applicable Ruggable, customer, regulatory, and performance standards.
• Proactively identify and resolve development, costing, quality, capacity, and manufacturing issues that could impact product launches.
• Conduct supplier and factory visits to evaluate capabilities, review product opportunities, manage development, and strengthen vendor partnerships.
• Maintain awareness of competitive assortments, consumer trends, emerging materials, manufacturing capabilities, and relevant developments within the home furnishings and textile markets.
• Drive continuous improvement within the white label development process, including supplier onboarding, product evaluation, sampling, costing, documentation, and cross-functional workflows.

What You’ll Need to Have:
Required:
• Bachelor’s degree in Product Development, Textiles, Merchandising, Sourcing, Business, or a related field; equivalent relevant industry experience may be considered.
• 5+ years of progressive product development, sourcing, or related experience, preferably within rugs, home textiles, home furnishings, or adjacent consumer product categories.
• Extensive experience working directly with overseas suppliers and factories.
• Demonstrated ability to identify and evaluate new vendors, manufacturing capabilities, and commercially viable product opportunities.
• Strong understanding of the product development and commercialization process from initial concept or product selection through production.
• Experience partnering closely with Creative, Design, and Merchandising teams to translate assortment needs into executable product solutions.
• Proven ability to manage multiple suppliers and development programs across complex timelines.
• Strong understanding of product costing, MOQs, lead times, supplier capabilities, and manufacturing considerations.
• Excellent project-management skills with a strong sense of urgency, organization, and attention to detail.
• Strong negotiation, communication, and relationship-management skills.
• Highly proactive and resourceful, with the ability to identify opportunities and solutions rather than relying solely on predetermined product briefs.
• Willingness to travel internationally to suppliers, factories, markets, and trade shows.
• Ability to work flexible hours as needed to communicate effectively with global suppliers across multiple time zones.

Preferred:
• Experience in sourcing rugs, home textiles, home furnishings, or related lifestyle products.
• Strong knowledge of global textile and home furnishings manufacturing regions and supplier capabilities.
• Established experience identifying and developing new overseas vendors.
• Understanding of textile materials, yarns, constructions, manufacturing processes, and finishing techniques.
• Familiarity with product testing, quality requirements, and relevant ASTM, AATCC, ISO, or other industry standards.
• Experience attending international trade shows, sourcing markets, and factory/vendor meetings.
• Experience with PLM systems, Airtable and project-management tools.

Compensation:
● $90,000-$105,000 per year base salary based on experience
● An annual bonus percentage that varies based on level of role
● Employer matching (up to 3% of base salary) for company sponsored 401K plan

This centralized role consolidates fleet maintenance management and rental operations into a single operational center of excellence. The Director owns lease/rental asset procurement specs, rate structures, fleet maintenance integration, and operational systems to maximize asset utilization and bottom-line profitability. We are looking for an energetic, solutions-oriented professional who thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment and is eager to grow with us.


Shift: Monday-Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m, normal business hours of operations.


What You’ll Do Day-to-Day (Essential Duties & Responsibilities):

  • Pricing & Rate Strategy: Establish and continuously refine corporate pricing guidelines, rental rate cards, and long-term full-service lease rate structures based on market conditions, asset cost, and maintenance history.
  • Fleet Utilization & Asset Allocation: Monitor daily, weekly, and monthly rental fleet utilization rates, strategically rebalancing equipment across locations to maximize revenue and meet regional demand.
  • Cross-Department Operational Alignment: Manage the operational intersection between the rental/lease fleet and service shop operations, ensuring preventative maintenance schedules, warranty work, and repairs are executed rapidly to minimize unit downtime.
  • Lifecycle & Asset Lifecycle Management: Monitor fleet age and total cost of operation, coordinating directly with the Used Truck team to determine optimal timing for retiring and transferring rental/lease units into used truck inventory.
  • High-Value Deal Support & Sales Enablement: Function as the corporate expert for regional Enterprise Sales Managers, assisting with complex deal structures, custom lease term calculations, and large fleet rental agreements.
  • Risk Management & Compliance: Ensure all lease and rental agreements comply strictly with corporate risk guidelines, liability protections, and maintenance allowance parameters.
  • Financial Performance Reporting: Deliver comprehensive monthly operational reports covering fleet yield, downtime metrics, maintenance spend per unit, and contract margin health.
  • Collaborate closely with team members and leadership to continuously cultivate positive experiences for our customers.
  • Perform other dynamic duties and responsibilities as assigned to support business.

What We’re Looking For (Qualifications & Skills):

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Transportation, Supply Chain Management, or a related field required. Significant equivalent industry experience will be fully considered in lieu of a formal degree.
  • 10 plus years of combined experience in commercial truck rental management, full-service leasing operations, or fleet maintenance leadership.
  • Proven experience managing multi-location commercial fleets, rental branch operations, or dealership service/maintenance infrastructure.
  • Strong command of fleet asset depreciation, maintenance costing, lease rate calculations, and rental yield metrics, preferred.
  • Comprehensive understanding of heavy-duty commercial truck components, preventative maintenance protocols, DOT compliance, and warranty processes, preferred.
  • Advanced proficiency in dealership Business Management Systems (BMS), rental/leasing management software, and data management tools (Google Workspace/Excel), preferred.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills to bridge technical maintenance requirements with regional sales leadership and corporate executive goals, preferred.
  • A curious mindset with an entrepreneurial "pioneering spirit," strong integrity, and a passion for continuous professional development.


What’s In It For You? (The Perks & Benefits)

We believe in taking care of our people. JX Enterprises offers a highly competitive compensation package designed to support your health, financial future, and overall well-being.


Ready to Drive Your Career Forward?

If you have a strong work ethic, a passion for learning, and are ready to contribute to a workplace where you are valued, we want to hear from you!

JOB TITLE: Web Application Developer


SUPERVISOR: Ocean Data Products (ODP) Program Director


Starting Salary Range: $75,000-$79,399


Overview:


The Gulf of Maine Research Institute (GMRI) develops and delivers collaborative solutions to global ocean challenges. We are dedicated to the resilience of the Gulf of Maine ecosystem and the communities that depend on it. To learn more, visit .


Ocean Data Products:


The primary role of the Ocean Data Products team at GMRI is to develop and support data management and cyberinfrastructure (DMAC) systems that provide access to real-time, historic, and forecast data in the northeast region through customized data products. ODP has served as the lead data management provider for NERACOOS (the Northeastern Regional Association for Coastal and Ocean Observing Systems) since the early 2000s. Additionally, ODP works with partners at GMRI and collaborators in the region developing products and data management infrastructure for fisheries, climate, and marine environmental data. Current projects include development of an infrastructure for meteorological and oceanographic data from offshore buoys and sensors, web based tools and dashboards for accessing water level data and model forecast visualizations, GMRI’s public-facing community science platform, and a data infrastructure for GMRI research data. The ODP team develops and supports web-based software and tools to access data and information about the marine environment. This team shares resources and project management duties as it facilitates and implements distributed data delivery systems to the ocean observing community and stakeholders interested in marine data.


Web Developer I:


The ODP team is looking an early career web developer to join the team. The Web Developer I position is a full-time regular position based on-site in Portland, ME with flexibility around hybrid work and reports to the ODP Program Director. The position is aimed toward candidates early in their career with growing skills and interest in one or more areas of specialization that will complement the skills of the current team, such as: back-end development, data acquisition and integration, or DevOps. The Web Developer I will provide ongoing support and contribute to the development of the suite of web-based software and tools used by stakeholders to access data and information about the marine environment. The Web Developer I will work closely with the ODP program director, ODP programmers, research scientists, stakeholders, and designers to support and maintain these systems. The person in this role will collaborate with internal partners at GMRI as well as external clients in the ocean observing, marine science, fisheries communities, and other stakeholders interested in marine data.


The ideal candidate for this position will have demonstrated knowledge and capacity to program web applications using industry standard programming languages, open source preferred. In addition, they will be an outstanding problem-solver with excellent coding skills, the ability to understand and work within a variety of software technologies, and the capacity to keep up to speed on industry trends and adapt to new technologies.

title: Director of Development
description:
Job Summary:

The Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health Office of Development and Alumni Relations (ODAR) is committed to securing the financial resources, time, and loyalty of alumni, friends, corporations, and foundations to promote the School’s work of educating new generations of global health leaders and producing powerful ideas that can transform the lives of people everywhere.

Reporting to the Managing Director of Development, the Director of Development (the Director) works within an entrepreneurial and dynamic School environment and closely collaborates with faculty, senior school administrators and University development colleagues to independently manage a portfolio of prospects who have the capacity to give $250,000 or more, secure funding for School priorities, and meet or exceed department revenue goals. The Director is responsible for identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding a portfolio of major gift prospects in assigned regions. The Director will also play a leadership role in the annual strategy planning process, take on additional related projects, and recommend strategies to enhance fundraising in collaboration with senior staff and Harvard Chan colleagues, as well as Alumni Affairs and Development more broadly at Harvard. The incumbent will represent Harvard Chan School at events, meetings, and off-site presentations and will engage in extensive travel to meet with prospects and donors.

This position will contribute to meeting and exceeding department revenue goals by developing and executing prospect strategies, cultivating and stewarding prospects and donors and directly soliciting gifts. This position will also advise and work closely with faculty, leaders in School departments, centers and/or research programs to further their fundraising strategy in alignment with broad School priorities. The successful candidate will be a team player who collaborates freely and builds trust with donors, alumni, friends and school partners, including but not limited to the Office of Communications, Office for Research Strategy and Development and the University Alumni Affairs and Development team.

Job-Specific Responsibilities:

  • Manages a portfolio of 100-125 prospects in assigned regions and at various stages of their relationship. Travels approximately 50% of the time (local Boston and nationally as assigned). Some international travel may be required pending portfolio assignments.
  • Develops appropriate cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategy to enhance retention, grow revenue, and improve donor advancement. Will be required to meet annual individual revenue and moves management goals.
  • - Makes a minimum of 100 visits annually. Qualifies, progresses, and cultivates newly identified prospects and evaluates major gift potential and next steps. As needed, utilizes email, digital, and phone outreach to meaningfully contact prospects outside of typical travel areas.
  • In collaboration with the University Planned Giving office, develops educational marketing materials for donors and prospects, and participates in internal team training on planned giving trends and tax implications. Ensures compliance with University polices and guidelines.
  • Coordinates closely with faculty and administrators to provide guidance on, and help implement, fundraising strategy.
  • Works strategically with volunteers to encourage them to build bridges and utilize their networks to help Harvard Chan School develop stronger relationships with other prominent alumni and friends.
  • Drafts briefings and correspondence for faculty and School leader, including the Dean.
  • Works with the Vice Dean, Managing Director and ODAR colleagues to strategize and plan development trips. Coordinates all aspects of development travel including prospect identification and follow-up correspondence. Drafts contact reports.
  • Staffs faculty or senior administrators in meetings with donors.
  • Works with prospect management and research to ensure research and due diligence is completed.
  • Works with the ODAR development communications staff to ensure talking points are written for the Dean or other senior administrators for speaking engagements.
  • Drafts gift proposals and other materials with support from development communications and donor relations staff as needed.
  • Works closely with other Major Gift Officers, Alumni Affairs and other ODAR colleagues in the development of on-campus events and programs that will lead to increased high-level involvement of alumni, donors and friends.

The above covers the most significant responsibilities of this position. It does not, however, exclude other duties, the inclusion of which would be in conformity with the level of the position.

PLEASE NOTE: This role will require approximately 50% travel, mostly domestically, but may have the opportunity for some international travel as well. The role may occasionally require evening and weekend work to ensure smooth execution of events.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience is required.
  • 8+ years of relevant experience is required.
  • Excellent communications skills, both oral and written.
  • Advanced understanding of fundraising. Work well in a busy office with competing demands; not easily flustered nor easily overwhelmed by a high volume of activity and projects.
  • Proven aptitude for successfully managing a robust portfolio, including setting priorities that enable meeting fundraising and visit goals.
  • Demonstrated track record in soliciting and closing six-and seven-figure gifts in a complex environment.
  • Experience working with a diverse constituency.
  • Strong knowledge of MS Office and experience learning new software quickly.

Additional Qualifications and Skills:

  • International fundraising experience is a plus.
  • Integrity and trust with a demonstrated knowledge in managing highly confidential information.
  • Aptitude for creative problem solving.
  • Proficiency in analyzing and explaining data.
  • Experience with planned giving terms and strategies and the knowledge for guiding, collaborating and advising colleagues in planned giving preferred.
  • Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week
  • Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position
  • Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Education

Join the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health to support our mission of health research and education, and to be a part of the oldest institution of higher learning in the country!

--------------------

--------------------

This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that some of the duties and responsibilities can be effectively performed at a non-Harvard location. The work schedule and location will be set by the department at its discretion and based upon operational needs. When not working at a Harvard or Harvard-designated location, employees in hybrid positions must work in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts. Additional details will be discussed during the interview process. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Establish a regular rhythm of inspection to analyze retention, churn, and growth causality to facilitate data-driven program improvements. Assemble and deliver executive reporting and meeting cadences to ensure seamless cross-functional alignment and accountability.   • Work in close concert with the GVP of Global Enterprise Customer Success and GVP of Global Commercial Customer Success and the Customer Value Program Director, to drive and execute a comprehensive program that ensures milestones, manages cross-functional dependencies and risks, and measures and impacts cross region and cross segment IAM adoption

title: Technical Writer
description:
Hos Gibotech bygger vi komplekse robot- og automationsløsninger, der får hospitaler og virksomheder til at fungere lidt smartere hver dag. Vores projekter spænder fra sterile forsyningssystemer til komplette produktionsanlæg, og fælles for dem alle er ønsket om at skabe løsninger, der virker i virkeligheden.

For at lykkes med det er det vigtigt, at alle dele spiller sammen, herunder også dokumentationen og brugsanvisningerne. På grund af fortsat høj aktivitet og en stærk ordretilgang udvider vi endnu en gang og søger en struktureret og kommunikativ Technical Writer, der kan omsætte komplekse tekniske oplysninger til klare og brugervenlige dokumenter. Du vil blive en del af vores QHSE, hvor du hvor du får en vigtig rolle i at gøre komplekst stof forståeligt og skabe struktur på tværs af fagområder. Kort sagt: du er med til at gøre vores tekniske fundament klart, brugbart og levende.

Dine arbejdsopgaver

Du bliver den, der får ordene og strukturen til at følge teknologien. Din hverdag handler om at omsætte teknisk viden til dokumentation, som både giver mening og værdi for dem, der bruger den – fra manualer og procedurer til online guides og specifikationsdokumenter.

Du vil blandt andet:

  • Udarbejde og vedligeholde brugsanvisninger, specifikationsdokumenter og tekniske dossierer
  • Hjælpe projektteams med at skabe overblik og sikre konsistens i deres dokumentation
  • Koordinere dokumentationsopgaver på tværs af projekter og afdelinger
  • Understøtte compliance og kvalitetsarbejde i henhold til standarder som ISO 9001
  • Være med til at udvikle og forbedre måden, vi arbejder med dokumentation og videndeling på

Hos os er dokumentation ikke et krav, men et redskab - et fælles sprog, der får teknologien til at hænge sammen.

Hvem er du?

Din uddannelsesmæssige baggrund er mindre afgørende – det vigtigste er, at du har en solid forståelse for systemer, processer eller produkter, fx inden for automation, mekanik eller software. Du er nysgerrig, systematisk og har en naturlig sans for at skabe orden i komplekse sammenhænge.

Vi forestiller os, at du:

  • Har erfaring med dokumentation og kvalitetssikring
  • Taler og skriver dansk og engelsk
  • Har en god forståelse for teknik
  • Arbejder selvstændigt og tager ansvar for dine opgaver
  • Er grundig, struktureret og detaljeorienteret
  • Er vant til at samarbejde på tværs af faggrupper
  • Har solid erfaring med MS Office

Du er typen, der kan se skønheden i en velstruktureret mappe og samtidig værdsætter den gode samtale med en kollega i huset.

Hvad du kan forvente hos os?

Hos Gibotech bliver du en del af et fagligt stærkt fællesskab, hvor teknologisk nysgerrighed, præcision og samarbejde går hånd i hånd – og hvor der er plads til grin i hverdagen. Vi løfter i flok og tror på, at de bedste løsninger skabes i et miljø med højt fagligt niveau og god stemning.

Du får ansvar og indflydelse på dine opgaver og er med hele vejen fra idé til drift. Vi arbejder tæt sammen på tværs af fagområder og står sammen, når løsningerne skal fungere i praksis – med fælles fokus på at skabe reel værdi for vores kunder.

Kulturen er uformel, tonen er direkte, og der er højt til loftet. Med base i Odense og projekter i både Danmark og udlandet tilbyder vi en varieret hverdag med tekniske udfordringer, stærkt kollegaskab, sociale arrangementer via personaleforeningen og heriblandt personalegoder som sodavand og morgenbrød.

Lyder det som noget for dig?

Så vil vi rigtig gerne høre fra dig. Send din ansøgning og dit CV – og hvis du har spørgsmål til stillingen eller til os som arbejdsplads, så tøv ikke med at tage fat i os.

Såfremt du har spørgsmål, er du velkommen til at kontakte

title: Commissioning Tuning Engineer
description:
Commissioning Tuning Engineer

Company Overview

At Mitsubishi Power, we're not just building better clean energy technologies; we're architecting a better future. Our team is boldly redefining power generation to accelerate the world's energy transition. We operate as one team, pushing toward our vision of the future. We value problem solvers, prioritize collaboration, and support each other in an inclusive culture built on accountability and authenticity by demonstrating our values: Safety, Family, Innovative, Inclusive, Accountable & Courageous. Together, we’re building the future we all aspire to - making net zero a reality.

Role Overview

The Commissioning Tuning Engineer applies advanced controls engineering expertise to the startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, maintenance, and optimization of Mitsubishi gas turbines. This role requires demonstrated experience in gas turbine controls and/or combustion tuning, with a strong understanding of turbine control systems and combustion dynamics. The engineer supports commissioning activities by diagnosing technical issues, optimizing turbine performance and reliability, and ensuring equipment operates safely and in accordance with required operational specifications.

Key Responsibilities
  • Demonstrates our core competencies: Action oriented, change champion, customer-focused, developing self & others, and ownership
  • Support gas turbine commissioning and startup, including operational verification, controls troubleshooting, and system readiness activities.
  • Independently perform combustion tuning on Mitsubishi J-Class gas turbines, including load overshoot mitigation, Fuel Gas Temperature (FGT) tuning, ignition tuning, and other advanced tuning procedures.
  • Apply expertise in combustion dynamics to diagnose and resolve combustion instabilities, pressure fluctuations, and other dynamic performance issues.
  • Utilize combustion tuning and diagnostic tools, including VB tuning programs and the Combustion Adjustment Support System (CASS), for data acquisition, analysis, and tuning adjustments.
  • Verify gas turbine control system functionality, including slot assignments, signal outputs, transmitters, failsafe logic, control loops, HMI displays, and overall system readiness.
  • Develop, implement, and troubleshoot DCS logic to support commissioning, controls operation, and combustion tuning activities.
  • Perform instrument loop checks, calculate operational setpoints, and validate control logic against system specifications and performance requirements.
  • Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective actions for technical and operational issues encountered during startup and commissioning.
  • Prepare accurate and timely technical reports documenting site conditions, actions taken, tuning results, and recommendations for performance improvement.
  • Complete required internal and customer-facing documentation associated with commissioning and combustion tuning activities.
Requirements
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering from an accredited four-year institution with 3+ years of relevant experience; or 5+ years of related experience/training; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Strong knowledge of combustion tuning processes and theory, with the technical understanding required to support gas turbine commissioning and tuning activities.
  • Strong analytical and technical interpretation skills, with the ability to read, analyze, and understand engineering documents, procedures, and technical requirements.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical information clearly to internal teams, customers, and stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in technical documentation, including preparation of reports, business correspondence, and technical procedures or manuals.
  • Proficiency with standard business and technical software, including databases, project management tools, spreadsheets, and word-processing applications.
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 70%, including domestic and international assignments by land and/or air for extended durations.
Why Should You Apply?
  • Excellent Benefits (Medical, Dental, Vision & 401K Matching).
  • Excellent development programs and advancement opportunities.
  • Tuition reimbursement and on-the-job training.
  • Paid vacation, sick time, and holidays.
  • Committed to quality products and services.
  • Great working environment and culture.
  • Employee Appreciation Programs and Event.

title: Staff Product Manager, Payments Transaction Risk
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
Join our mission

Intuit is a global technology platform that helps our customers and communities overcome their most important financial challenges. We serve over 50 million consumer, small business, and self-employed customers worldwide — powering the money movement behind QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and TurboTax.

Overview

Every bill payment and payroll disbursement we process is a real-time risk decision: release funds so vendors and employees get paid on time, and stop fraud and financial loss before it happens. Getting this right — minimizing losses while not delaying good money movement with false holds — directly moves the P&L and whether a small business can operate.

We're hiring a Staff Product Manager who owns our bill payment and payroll transaction risk outcomes — accountable for hitting fiscal-year loss-reduction and insult-reduction (false-positive) goals. You'll own both the strategy and the capabilities to get there: the risk decisioning approach, the data science models, the data vendors, and the counterparty risk signals that power fast, accurate decisions.

This is a technical, results-driven role for someone who has built risk decisioning strategies before and wants to push them to the next generation with AI and richer data. Our partners are cross-functional, globally distributed, and domain experts. Success demands customer obsession, innovative solutions, and analytical rigor in equal measure.


Responsibilities

How you will lead

  • Own the number. Set and deliver the strategy to achieve fiscal year goals for loss reduction and insult-rate (false-positive) reduction across bill payment and payroll transaction risk — you are accountable for the outcome, not just the roadmap.

  • Own the risk decisioning strategy. Decide how models, rules, and signals combine to approve good transactions and stop bad ones in real time, tuning the balance between loss and customer insult.

  • Expand the data foundation. Evaluate, integrate, and operationalize new data vendors and internal sources; own data quality, coverage, and cost trade-offs in service of decision accuracy.

  • Build counterparty risk signals. Develop features and signals that assess the risk of transaction counterparties (payees, vendors, employees, contractors) and the relationships between them.

  • Advance real-time, AI-native decisioning — latency, reliability, explainability, and the guardrails governing automated decisions.

  • Own the scoreboard and communicate it. Instrument and report loss rates, false-positive rates, approval/decline rates, model precision/recall and lift, and decision latency; align leaders on trade-offs and progress to goal.

  • Align and deliver across data science, engineering, risk policy, compliance, and operations; ruthlessly prioritize and set delivery timelines.


Qualifications

What you'll bring

  • 4+ years in Product Management, including sustained ownership of complex, technical, multi-team initiatives with accountability for measurable business outcomes.

  • Proven track record building risk/fraud decisioning strategies — you've owned loss and/or false-positive outcomes on risk scoring, transaction monitoring, underwriting, or fraud-prevention products, and understand the dynamics of financial risk.

  • Deep partnership with data science / ML teams — you've helped develop, evaluate, and productionize models, and reason fluently about features, precision/recall, and model trade-offs.

  • Experience with data vendors and data pipelines — evaluating, integrating, and operationalizing third-party and internal data for decisioning.

  • Strong technical fluency: real-time/streaming decisioning, APIs, data infrastructure, and experimentation

  • Quantitative rigor: comfortable with analytics and A/B testing to size opportunities, set targets, and prove impact against goals.

  • Experience in payments, fraud, risk, or another high-scale financial domain

  • Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree or MBA preferred.


Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

title: OneStream Federal Data Architect
description:
Andrew Morgan LLC (AM) is a fast-growing Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business. We are currently seeking a qualified OneStream Federal Data Architect to join our team supporting our Federal Client.

As a OneStream Federal Data Architect, you will design, build, and sustain the data foundation for enterprise financial management solutions supporting federal clients, including the Department of War and Federal Civilian Agencies. The Data Architect will lead the design of data integration strategies, ETL pipelines, and dimensional structures that feed OneStream budget formulation, execution, and reporting processes. This role requires deep technical expertise in OneStream data management combined with a strong understanding of federal financial data, source systems, and the budget lifecycle.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Design and maintain the end-to-end data architecture for OneStream implementations, including dimensional models, data sources, transformation rules, and integration workflows aligned to federal budget and appropriation structures.
  • Develop, optimize, and document ETL processes that extract, transform, and load data from federal financial and ERP systems (e.g., GFEBS, DAI, Oracle, SAP, Momentum or legacy accounting systems) into OneStream.
  • Build and manage OneStream Data Management jobs, Connectors, Workflow profiles, and transformation rule sets to ensure accurate, timely, and auditable data loads.
  • Author and maintain business rules and scripts (VB.NET and/or C#) and SQL queries supporting data integration, validation, and automation.
  • Establish data quality, reconciliation, and validation controls that support audit readiness and traceability of financial data from source to report.
  • Map federal financial data elements, including appropriations, program elements, funds, object classes, and cost centers, into OneStream metadata and dimension hierarchies.
  • Collaborate with functional leads, budget analysts, and client stakeholders to translate business requirements into scalable technical data designs.
  • Produce technical documentation, including data flow diagrams, interface control documents, mapping specifications, and runbooks for sustainment teams.
  • Support performance tuning, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis for data load and integration issues across development, test, and production environments.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to developers and analysts and contribute to design reviews and architectural decisions.

REQUIREMENTS:

  • At least 8 years of total professional experience in data architecture, data engineering, ETL development, or enterprise performance management (EPM) solutions.
  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing data integrations within OneStream (via REST API, SFTP, ODBC, Smart Integration Connector-SIC, Flat files), including Data Management, Connectors, transformation rules, and Workflow.
  • Demonstrated ETL experience using tools such as OneStream Data Management, SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS), Informatica, Azure Data Factory, or comparable platforms.
  • Strong proficiency in SQL and relational database design, with experience in Microsoft SQL Server or similar environments.
  • Experience developing OneStream business rules in VB.NET or C#.
  • Experience supporting federal government clients, preferably within DoW, 4th Estate or Federal Civilian Agencies.
  • Working knowledge of federal financial management concepts, including appropriations, budget formulation and execution, and the PPBE process.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
  • U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust or Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • OneStream OCA or OCP Certification
  • Familiarity with DoW financial systems and data standards, including the Standard Line of Accounting (SLOA) and audit readiness requirements (FIAR).
  • Experience with cloud data platforms (Azure preferred) and API-based integrations.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Finance, or a related field; advanced degree a plus.

SALARY:

Salary is commensurate with both location and experience.

THE AM EMPLOYEE WILL DISPLAY…

  • Attention to Detail: Produce high-quality deliverables and outputs that align with contract outcomes.
  • Self-Sufficiency: Execute tasks independently, seeking client assistance only after internal resources are exhausted, ensuring requests align with contract goals.
  • Teamwork: Collaborate effectively with team members, including AMC resources, subcontractors, and government stakeholders.
  • Communication/Engagement: Maintain professional conduct in meetings and written communication, participating actively with cameras on.
  • Responsiveness: Stay engaged, communicate promptly, and ensure deadlines are consistently met.

ABOUT ANDREW MORGAN…

Andrew Morgan LLC, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Alexandria, VA, is a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) and a certified HUBZone Small Business. We specialize in delivering high-quality consulting services to both federal and commercial clients, offering expertise in Strategy and Management Consulting, Technology & Architecture Services, and Industry & Mission Analytics Solutions. Our distinguished clientele includes the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the Department of Defense (DoD), and the United Stated Army Corps of Engineers (USACE). We are committed to providing innovative solutions and exceptional service to support our clients' missions and objectives.

At Anduril, our Battlespace Awareness Command and Control Software team specializes in solving complex, real-world problems through cutting-edge algorithms and intelligent software integrations. Operating in small, innovative teams, we push the boundaries of what's possible to deliver advanced technologies with mission-critical applications. We are currently seeking talented technologists to join our mission and redefine the future of defense technology.

About the Job

We are looking to hire an Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer to join our growing Battlespace Awareness team. This role owns the CI/CD and integration test infrastructure that keeps our command and control (C2) software reliable as it scales, and supports the observability stack — dashboards, metrics, and data pipelines that gives engineers and customers visibility into system health. You'll maintain what's running in production today and help lead the team's migration to next-generation infrastructure tooling.

Support integration test CI/CD infrastructure

  • Help lead the team's infrastructure using: Terraform, RKE2, ArgoCD, alongside traditional DevOps work (build systems, environment provisioning, release engineering).

  • Experience with Amazon Web Services (AWS) and ArgoCD

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Helm, Terraform, RKE2, ArgoCD.
  • Experience with Robot Framework testing.
  • Familiarity with Data Lake architectures and tooling for metrics pipelines.
  • Familiarity with MCAP data and Foxglove
  • Familiarity with Rust, C, or C++.
  • Familiarity with team collaboration tooling such as Slack and Slackbot CI development

title: AI Risk Evaluator
description:
Do you want to work on AI risk management in one of the leading financial institutions in the Nordics?
Join Danske Bank's newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management, operating as a central 1st Line of Defence capability. You will help build a consistent, evidence-based approach to assessing AI models and AI-enabled solutions across the Bank. As an AI Risk Evaluator, you will assess solutions before deployment and throughout their lifecycle, helping Model Owners and development teams demonstrate that intended use, performance, limitations, risks and controls are understood, tested and documented. This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of cutting-edge AI technologies, risk ownership, control execution and financial regulation.

Who are we?
The AI Model Assessment team is a central 1st Line of Defence capability responsible for supporting the identification, assessment, mitigation and monitoring of risks arising from AI solutions across the Bank. We work closely with Model Owners, business units, data scientists, engineers, model developers and governance functions to translate risk and control requirements into practical assessments, testing and traceable evidence.
Our mission is to enable innovation while helping the business fulfil its responsibility to manage AI model risk and deploy AI systems in a safe, robust and well-governed manner.

What you will be doing

As an AI Risk Evaluator, you will operate within the Bank's 1st Line of Defence, performing lifecycle assessments that help Model Owners and business areas exercise their accountability for AI model risk, execute effective controls, address weaknesses and maintain decision-useful evidence. You will provide assessment evidence and respond to objective challenge from relevant 2nd Line of Defence function, which retain responsibility for oversight and, where applicable, validation.

Your responsibilities will include:
• Conducting assessments of foundation models, GenAI applications, AI agents, and traditional machine learning models.
• Understanding the business process, intended use, technical architecture, human oversight and potential impact of a solution as the basis for an appropriate evaluation.
• Translating identified risk and control requirements into testable evaluation objectives, metrics, datasets and acceptance criteria.
• Providing robust challenge to use-case owners, model developers and other stakeholders regarding assumptions, risks, controls and evaluation evidence.
• Designing and executing evaluations covering model performance, robustness, hallucination and grounding, harmful behaviour, prompt injection, overreliance and other relevant failure modes.
• Assessing the quality, representativeness and limitations of evaluation data; identifying risks and control weaknesses; and producing clear, traceable findings and recommendations to support risk acceptance, governance and deployment decisions.
• Contributing evaluation findings to reusable methodologies, test assets and minimum assessment standards.
• Preparing complete and reproducible assessment evidence for independent review, challenge and, where applicable, validation by relevant Second Line of Defence functions.
• Supporting Model Owners and development teams in addressing findings, strengthening controls and reassessing solutions following material changes or identified issues.

This position can be based in Copenhagen, Denmark, Vilnius, Lithuania, Warsaw, Poland, Stockholm, Sweden or Helsinki, Finland.

About you

An experienced AI or machine learning professional with a strong understanding of AI technologies and the risks they introduce.
Ideally, you have:
• Extensive experience working with AI, machine learning, model validation, model risk management, AI governance, or a related field.
• Strong understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs), foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, and modern AI architectures.
• Ability to connect technical findings with enterprise risks, controls, business processes and governance decisions.
• Experience evaluating AI systems from a technical and risk perspective.
• Familiarity with AI evaluation methodologies and benchmarking frameworks.
• Experience using Python for data analysis, model testing, or experimentation.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to engage both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Curiosity, critical thinking, and the confidence to challenge assumptions.

Experience from financial services or regulated industries is an advantage.

Candidates from strong applied AI or technical evaluation backgrounds who can demonstrate an understanding of enterprise risk and controls are also encouraged to apply.

What we offer you

You will join a newly established AI Model Assessment team that is building the Bank's central capability for AI model assessment.
The team combines deep technical AI expertise with practical risk and control capabilities and works on some of the Bank's most strategic AI initiatives. We collaborate across the organisation, including with independent Second Line of Defence functions, and continuously evolve our methodologies as AI technologies and governance expectations mature.
This is an opportunity to help define how AI risk is managed at scale in one of the most advanced AI environments in the Nordic financial sector.

If hired in Lithuania, your monthly salary would range from 3680 EUR to 5520 EUR gross (based on your competencies relevant for the job).
Additionally, each Danske Bank employee receives employee benefits package which includes:
• Growth opportunities: professional & supportive team, e-learnings, numerous development programs; (incl. professional certificates); 100+ professions for internal mobility opportunities.
• Health & Well-being: a diverse, inclusive, work & life balance work environment; additional health insurance; mental well-being practices; partial psychologist counselling compensation; silence and sleep zones at the office; game rooms.
• Hybrid working conditions: Work from home up to two days a week; home office budget (after the probation period); modern Danske Campus workplace developed with anthropologist for the best employee experience.
• Additional days of leave: for rest, health, volunteering, exams in higher education institutions, and other important activities. Moreover, for seniority with Danske Bank.
• Monetary compensation package: accidents & critical diseases insurance; financial support in case of unfortunate events, travel insurance; IIIrd Pillar Pension Fund contribution.

See all the benefits HERE.
Your job function (position) in the job contract will be AI Science

Are you ready for the next step?

If you are passionate about understanding how AI works, identifying its risks, and helping organisations deploy AI safely and responsibly, we would love to hear from you.
For questions about the role, please contact Khaled Alizai Head of AI Model Assessmentat khali@danskebank.dk.
Join us and help grow the AI Model Assessment team at Danske Bank. We’ll be screening the applications on an ongoing basis so we encourage you to apply.

description:
COACH JOB DESCRIPTION

Chadwick School

Palos Verdes Peninsula, California

Chadwick School is an independent, K-12, coeducational day school dedicated to academic excellence, the development of exemplary character, and self-discovery through experience. A highly educated faculty and staff bring out the best in the talented student body through active learning, challenging academics, one-on-one mentoring, unparalleled global opportunities, nationally distinguished outdoor education and community service programs, outstanding athletic opportunities, and award-winning visual and performing arts.

The core values of respect, responsibility, honesty, fairness, and compassion are widely shared and fostered daily in classrooms, during co-curricular activities, and through the camaraderie of this close-knit community.

Located on a beautiful, 45-acre hilltop campus on the scenic Palos Verdes Peninsula in Los Angeles County, Chadwick enrolls over 800 students drawn from more than 45 Southern California communities.

Founded in 1935 by visionary educator Margaret Lee Chadwick, Chadwick is one of two schools operated by the Roessler-Chadwick Foundation. In 2010, Chadwick International School was formed in Songdo, South Korea, which expanded opportunities for students around the globe to benefit from a world-class Chadwick education.

Job Title: Walk On Athletics Coach

Division/Department: Athletics

Reports To: Director of Athletics

Location: Palos Verdes Peninsula, CA

Level/Grade: Middle School

Type of position/FLSA: Response

Compensation $21.00 - $30.00 hourly - based on experience and qualifications

POSITION SUMMARY

Chadwick School seeks an enthusiastic Middle School Athletics Coach to lead and mentor young student-athletes in fundamental skill development, teamwork, sportsmanship, and character building. The ideal candidate understands the unique developmental, emotional, and physical needs of middle school students (grades 6–8). The Middle School Coach fosters an inclusive, high-energy environment where participation, fundamental growth, effort, and enjoyment of the sport are prioritized alongside competitive spirit.

REQUIRED WORK TIME & HOURS

This is a part-time seasonal position requiring presence during scheduled practice times and competitive contests throughout the sports season. Minimum 10hours per week during season:

  • Monday – Thursday Practices: Start at 1:50 PM.
  • Friday Practices: 12:30 PM – 1:10 PM.
  • Game Days: After-school games during the week as scheduled (end times vary depending on game location, travel, and competition duration).

ASSOCIATED RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Skill & Strategy Development: Plan and conduct age-appropriate practices that focus on fundamental mechanics, core sport tactics, rules, and athletic conditioning tailored to middle school skill levels.
  • Positive Culture & Youth Mentorship: Model and teach Chadwick’s core values of respect, responsibility, honesty, fairness, and compassion. Promote dynamic teamwork, balanced play, and constructive feedback.
  • Game & Roster Management: Manage game situations, ensure fair playing time opportunities aligned with Middle School Athletics guidelines, track stats, and adjust strategies dynamically.
  • Safety & Student Supervision: Provide direct supervision of middle school student-athletes at all times during practices, games, locker room prep, campus transitions, and team travel.
  • Vertical Program Alignment: Coordinate with Upper School Head Coaches to align foundational technical skills, terminology, and tactical principles for smooth athletic progression into high school sports.
  • Parent & Department Communication: Maintain prompt, clear, and professional communication with middle school parents, student-athletes, and the Athletic Department.
  • Equipment & Facility Care: Assist in setting up facilities, maintaining sport-specific gear, managing team uniforms, and supervising proper cleanup post-practice/game.
  • Inclusion & Social Justice: Proactively participate in discussions and practices around identity, social justice, and inclusive community building within middle school athletics.
  • Policies & Training: Attend required coaching meetings, complete middle school CPR/First Aid certification, and follow all guidelines in the Employee & Athletic Handbooks.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

title: Tech Lead – Infrastructure
description:
Can you own the platform and pipelines that EIVA’s software is built on?

EIVA is an equipment and software engineering company delivering solutions to the international maritime industry. Our customers operate within renewable energy, oil & gas exploration, seabed-to-surface construction and hydrographic surveying – often in demanding environments where timing, precision and safety margins matter.

You do not need to know the subsea domain to apply. Here, your product is the software itself, and your users are the other engineering teams who build and ship on the platform you own. What matters is curiosity – the ability to ask the right questions and translate what you hear into good technical decisions – and a collaborative, team-first mindset.

The position is based at EIVA’s Danish office in Stilling (just one minute from the E45, approximately 15 minutes from Aarhus by car and easily accessible by bus).

What's involved?

As Tech Lead – Infrastructure, you'll own the platform, pipelines and infrastructure that our NaviSuite software is built on.

Around 80% of the role is hands-on: working directly in the team's technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and tooling. The rest is technical leadership – owning architecture within the Infrastructure team, making the final call on anything inside the team's decision domain, and knowing when a question needs to go further, to our architects or to alignment with other teams. You'll also help keep that decision domain itself well defined: what the team can decide on its own, and where it needs external alignment.

There could be occasional travel – around one to two short trips a year.

Your responsibilities…

  • Doing hands-on development and engineering work across the team's core technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and internal tooling (around 80% of the role)
  • Making the final technical decisions within the team's decision domain, and helping define where that domain's boundaries sit versus where the team needs external alignment
  • Securing technical quality in the team – code and infrastructure-as-code review, best practices, testing and automation standards
  • Owning architecture in the team – ensuring platform and pipeline work aligns with EIVA's overall architecture, and explaining the interdependencies to the team
  • Participating in refinement, securing that features, stories and tasks describe architectural dependencies, feasibility, quality requirements and operational aspects such as reliability, security, cost and developer experience
  • Cross team alignment – representing the Infrastructure team's technical position and making sure its work fits with adjacent work elsewhere in the organisation
  • Driving clarification with architects on technical questions that sit outside the team's decision domain

Also part of the role…

  • Providing technical mentoring and sparring for the team's engineers
  • Supporting the other development teams as users of the platform – helping with adoption, guidance and acting on their feedback
  • Taking operational responsibility for the platform and pipelines
  • Keeping the team's technical practices current – seeking out training, evaluating new tooling and sharing that knowledge internally
  • Maintaining technical documentation for the platform, pipelines and environments
  • Giving technical input to hiring and onboarding new engineers on the team
  • Giving technical input to estimation and planning together with the Team Manager/Product Owner

The ideal candidate…

  • Has a background in software engineering or computer science
  • Has hands-on experience building and maintaining platforms, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code and internal tooling
  • Has experience managing complex DevOps systems and workflows, and is comfortable making final technical calls within a defined decision domain
  • Is familiar with tools such as Git/GitHub, artifact storage, Ansible and Terraform
  • Has a collaborative mindset – comfortable gathering feedback from stakeholders across teams and using it to design clean, well-reasoned solutions
  • Is a team player who's good at knowledge-sharing and educating peers, and takes proactive ownership of their domain
  • It's a bonus if you also have experience with licence management systems, but not a requirement.

Joining the EIVA crew

At EIVA, you'll join a team that values openness, informality and collaboration – while working with high-end, innovative technology in an inspiring environment. We appreciate personal responsibility and proactivity, and there is room to make your mark if you spot new opportunities. Work-life balance matters to us and is reflected in the 15th, 20th and even 25th work anniversaries commonly celebrated at EIVA. We offer…

  • A pension scheme and health insurance
  • A canteen that no one leaves hungry
  • An active social calendar

Ready to dive in?

If this sounds like your kind of ownership, we'd love to hear from you. In your application, please tell us about a DevOps solution you've built that you're most proud of.

We review applications and hold interviews on a rolling basis until we find the right person, so don't wait for a deadline to apply. We're aiming for a start by 1 November.

For more information, please contact Joseph Sondergaard Daley, Manager, Autonomy Services – Software Development, at jsd@eiva.com.

Learn more about EIVA

title: Thermal Sciences Associate - Aircraft Systems/Performance (Ph.D.)
description:
About Exponent

Exponent is the only premium engineering and scientific consulting firm with the depth and breadth of expertise to solve our clients’ most profoundly unique, unprecedented, and urgent challenges.

Our vision is to engage multidisciplinary teams of science, engineering, and regulatory experts to empower clients with solutions that create a safer, healthier, more sustainable world. Join our team of experts with degrees from top programs at over 500 universities and extensive experience spanning a variety of industries. At Exponent, you’ll contribute to the diverse pool of ideas, talents, backgrounds, and experiences that drives our collaborative teamwork and breakthrough insights. Plus, we help you grow your career through mentoring, sponsorship, and a culture of learning. Thanks for your interest in joining our team!

Key statistics:

  • 950+ Consultants
  • 640+ Ph.D.s
  • 90+ Disciplines
  • 30+ Offices globally

Our Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Thermal Sciences Associate with a focus on aircraft systems and performance for our Thermal Sciences Practice in New York, NY. You will be responsible for applying fundamental engineering and scientific techniques to real-world problems in failure analysis and risk mitigation.

You will be responsible for

  • Applying fundamental principles of thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, combustion, dynamics and aerospace engineering to investigate complex technical problems involving aircraft, propulsion systems, and other thermal-fluid systems
  • Analyzing and distilling complex data
  • Conducting site, aircraft, and component inspections, and documenting physical evidence
  • Performing laboratory experiments and analytical or computational modeling
  • Evaluating the design, operation, performance, and failure modes of aircraft and including gas turbines, turbomachinery, fuel delivery systems, combustion systems, and associated controls.
  • Reviewing and understanding experiments and simulations performed by clients
  • Researching and parsing data from published literature
  • Conducting risk assessments
  • Preparing written reports, proposals, and presentations that communicate complex engineering findings to attorneys, clients, regulators, engineers, and other technical and non-technical audiences
  • Managing projects and maintaining efficiency under deadlines
  • Expanding technical expertise through research, publications conference participation, and continued engagement with developments in thermal sciences, aircraft systems, propulsion, aviation safety, and aerospace engineering

You will have the following skills and qualifications

  • Ph.D. in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aeronautics and Astronautics, or a related field, with a practical and theoretical understanding of thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, and combustion
  • Presently legally authorized to work in the United States. No immigration sponsorship or processing required.
  • Understanding of aircraft and/or spacecraft systems and performance, such as control systems, flight controls, propulsion systems, instrumentation, environmental control systems, automated flight-control systems, cockpit controls, and the interaction between pilot inputs and aircraft response
  • Outstanding ability to apply fundamental engineering concepts to new problems
  • Hands-on experience designing and executing experimental programs
  • An understanding of modeling and simulating aircraft and/or systems
  • Ability to interpret technical documentation including, but not limited to, flight manuals, operating procedures, system schematics, maintenance records, performance charts, engineering drawings, and test data
  • Interest in investigating system failures, abnormal operating conditions, accidents, performance anomalies, or equipment malfunctions
  • Familiarity with FAA regulations, certification requirements, and piloting and aircraft operations
  • Aircraft accident investigation experience is a plus, but not required
  • Willingness and ability to travel (<10%)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Applicants are encouraged to submit a CV (Curriculum Vitae) with publications (feel free to include publications that are in review or pending) [not restricted to 1 page].

In our offices, you can expect a supportive culture and a collaborative, dynamic, multi-disciplinary work environment. title: Senior Engineer, Manufacturing Equipment Engineering
description:
As a Senior Equipment Engineer specializing in sputter media, you will be responsible for leading equipment sustaining, reliability, and continuous improvement activities to support high-volume hard disk media manufacturing. You will play a key role in driving equipment performance, improving operational efficiency, and supporting new technology implementation. This role requires strong technical leadership to guide technicians in maintaining stable manufacturing operations, reducing equipment downtime, and enabling next-generation product and process requirements.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead day-to-day equipment sustaining activities, including troubleshooting, failure analysis, and resolution of equipment-related production issues.
  • Drive equipment reliability improvement initiatives to enhance equipment uptime, reduce chronic failures, and improve overall operational stability.
  • Develop, implement, and optimize preventive and predictive maintenance strategies to improve long-term equipment performance.
  • Lead root cause analysis (RCA) for major equipment failures and implement effective corrective and preventive actions.
  • Support equipment upgrades, hardware modifications, and machine conversion activities to meet product and technology roadmap requirements.
  • Coordinate new equipment installation, commissioning, qualification, and acceptance to ensure systems meet operational and safety standards.
  • Monitor and analyze equipment performance indicators such as OEE, MTBF, MTTR, and downtime trends to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Collaborate closely with Process Engineering, Yield Engineering, Production, and Quality teams to improve process capability and manufacturing performance.
  • Drive engineering projects related to equipment improvements, automation enhancement, and productivity optimization.
  • Develop and maintain equipment documentation including SOPs, maintenance procedures, troubleshooting guides, and best practices.
  • Work closely with OEM vendors and suppliers to resolve technical issues, implement upgrades, and support equipment technology development.
  • Support cost reduction initiatives through engineering optimization, reliability improvements, and maintenance efficiency.
  • Ensure all equipment operations comply with company safety policies, regulatory requirements, and industry standards.
  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives, including Lean manufacturing, automation deployment, and digitalization programs.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned by management.

REQUIRED:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronic, Materials Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Minimum 5–8 years of experience in equipment engineering within semiconductor, sputter media, vacuum coating, or advanced manufacturing industries.
  • Strong understanding of vacuum systems, sputtering equipment, and manufacturing equipment control systems.
  • Experience in equipment troubleshooting, reliability improvement, and manufacturing support.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to perform data analysis and technical investigations.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and ability to present technical information clearly.
  • Ability to work effectively in a cross-functional manufacturing environment.

PREFERRED:

  • Experience in a sputter media or semiconductor manufacturing environment.
  • Knowledge of high-vacuum technology, plasma processes, or thin-film deposition systems.
  • Experience with equipment automation, PLC systems, and equipment control interfaces.

SKILLS:

  • Strong knowledge of vacuum systems and thin-film deposition equipment, including troubleshooting and performance optimization.
  • Experience with PLC systems, automation control, and equipment interface systems.
  • Ability to perform equipment failure analysis and implement reliability improvement actions.
  • Good understanding of Statistical Process Control (SPC), equipment data analysis, and performance monitoring.
  • Strong collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively with engineers, technicians, and cross-functional teams.
  • Good communication skills to clearly explain technical issues and solutions to different levels of the organization.
  • Ability to manage multiple technical tasks and support fast-paced manufacturing operations.
  • Strong technical documentation and reporting skills.

title: QA Inspector (ICC Certified) – Commercial Building Codes/Modular Construction
description:
Help Raise the Standard for Modular Construction Quality

NFPA Global Solutions is expanding our Manufactured Structures team and is seeking experienced ICC-certified Quality Auditors who are passionate about building code compliance, construction quality, and working directly with manufacturers.


This role offers the opportunity to apply your inspection and code expertise while supporting manufacturers throughout your assigned territory. You'll spend much of your time visiting local manufacturing facilities, building strong relationships with customers, and ensuring products meet the highest standards for quality and code compliance. While travel is a regular part of the position, most travel is local, with overnight travel averaging up to 25%.

If you're looking for a role that combines technical expertise, independence, and meaningful customer interaction, we'd love to hear from you.


What You'll Do

  • Review production records, inspection documentation, and quality management systems.
